import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Pseudorandom

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Private-key encryption: single- and multi-message security

The computational definitions of secure private-key encryption of [PS10, §2.1.3, §3.5–§3.7]
on top of the machine layer `Complexity.NUPPT` (foundation decisions D3–D6 of
`PassShelatChapter2-4Plan.md`): an *efficient private-key encryption scheme* is a triple of
PPTs `(Gen, Enc, Dec)` with perfect correctness [PS10, Definition 24.7]; it is
*single-message secure* when the encryptions of any two messages are computationally
indistinguishable [PS10, Definition 91.1] and *multi-message secure* when the encryptions of
any two vectors of polynomially many messages under one key are [PS10, Definition 93.1].
The section's construction is the one-time pad with a pseudorandom pad
[PS10, Algorithm 92.1], secure by the four-hybrid argument [PS10, Theorem 92.2], and the
section's impossibility result is that a deterministic (stateless) scheme is never
multi-message secure [PS10, Theorem 94.2].

The file has the two layers of D2.

* **Concrete** (one `n`, samplers and adversaries as functions of uniform coins): the
  truncated one-time pad `padXor` (an `n`-bit message masked by the first `n` bits of an
  `L`-bit pad), its perfect secrecy `acceptProb_padXor` (Claim-92.a: `m ⊕ U` is uniform, so
  `m₀ ⊕ U` and `m₁ ⊕ U` are identically distributed), and the exact four-hybrid bound
  `distAdv_padXor_le`: a distinguisher of `m₀ ⊕ G(U_n)` from `m₁ ⊕ G(U_n)` has advantage at
  most the sum of two PRG advantages `prgAdv G (D ∘ (mᵢ ⊕ ·))` [PS10, Theorem 92.2, proof].
* **Asymptotic**: `PrivateKeyScheme`, `SingleMessageSecure`, `MultiMessageSecure`, the
  scheme `prgScheme` of Algorithm 92.1 as a `PrivateKeyScheme` value built from
  `Complexity.NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform` of the FP functions `pairSndD` (the key is the coin
  string) and `prgPadFun` (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairXor`), its correctness proved,
  its security `prgScheme_singleMessageSecure` proved by the four-hybrid argument (the
  message pair hard-wired as advice, `Complexity.NUPPT.exists_withAdvice`), and
  Theorem 94.2 proved (`not_multiMessageSecure_of_deterministic`) with the text's two-message
  distinguisher `[c₀ = c₁]` (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairEq`).

**Deviation:** `PrivateKeyScheme`: messages at parameter `n` are the `n`-bit strings
(the text's `m ∈ {0,1}^n`), keys and ciphertexts arbitrary strings; `Enc` and `Dec` are
activated at parameter `n` on `⟨1^n, ⟨k, ·⟩⟩` (time polynomial in `n`; the text's "polynomial
in the size of their inputs" agrees since `|k| ≤ poly(n)`); correctness holds for every coin
string of `Gen`, `Enc` and `Dec` (the probability-one reading of [PS10, Definition 24.6],
`Complexity.NUPPT.computes_iff_uprob`); `Dec`'s `⊥` is any output that does not decode to an
`n`-bit string (`decodeFin`).

**Deviation:** `SingleMessageSecure`, `MultiMessageSecure`: the distinguisher receives `1^n`
with the ciphertext(s) (D5); the bound is `≤ ε(n)` (the text's "at most"); the `q(n) + 1`
ciphertexts of Definition 93.1 are encoded as a nested pair `encodeList`.

**Deviation:** `prgScheme` (Algorithm 92.1): the key is an `n`-bit seed and the pad is the
first `n` bits of `G(k)` (the text's `n/2`-bit key for a length-doubling `G` requires `n`
even; with syntactic polynomial lengths (D9) a key length that is a non-constant function of
the message length is never shorter than the message, so the "short key" economy of §3.6 is a
matter of parametrization and the security argument, the four hybrids, is unchanged); the
evaluator `F` of `G` is an explicit argument rather than extracted from `PRG.Easy`.

**Deviation:** `not_multiMessageSecure_of_deterministic` (Theorem 94.2): "stateless" is built
into the model (an `NUPPT` has no state between activations); "deterministic" is
`PrivateKeyScheme.Deterministic` (the output of `Enc` does not depend on its coins); the
proof uses correctness (to get `c'₀ ≠ c'₁`) and `n ≥ 1` (two distinct messages), both
implicit in the text.

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.PrivateKeyScheme` — an efficient private-key encryption scheme
  [PS10, Definition 24.7]; `PrivateKeyScheme.encDist` — `{k ← Gen(1^n) : Enc_k(m)}`;
  `PrivateKeyScheme.multiEncDist`, `PrivateKeyScheme.encodeList` — the vector of
  `q + 1` encryptions under one key.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.PrivateKeyScheme.SingleMessageSecure` — [PS10, Definition 91.1].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.PrivateKeyScheme.MultiMessageSecure` — [PS10, Definition 93.1].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.PrivateKeyScheme.Deterministic` — `Enc` ignores its coins.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.padXor` — the truncated one-time pad `m ⊕ p|_n`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.prgPadFun`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.prgScheme` — the scheme of
  [PS10, Algorithm 92.1].

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.acceptProb_padXor` — perfect secrecy of the one-time pad (Claim-92.a).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.distAdv_padXor_le` — the concrete four-hybrid bound of
  [PS10, Theorem 92.2].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.prgScheme_encDist` — the ciphertext distribution of Algorithm 92.1 is
  `m ⊕ G(U_n)|_n`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.prgScheme_singleMessageSecure` — [PS10, Theorem 92.2].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.PrivateKeyScheme.not_multiMessageSecure_of_deterministic` —
  [PS10, Theorem 94.2].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.PrivateKeyScheme.MultiMessageSecure.singleMessageSecure` —
  multi-message security implies single-message security (the sanity direction of
  [PS10, §3.7, "extends"]).

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§2.1.3: Definition 24.7; §3.5: Definition 91.1; §3.6: Algorithm 92.1, Theorem 92.2;
  §3.7: Definition 93.1, Theorem 94.2.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.2–3.3 (the concrete `distAdv`, `prgAdv`, Lemma 3.2).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Complexity Turing Finset

/-! ### Transporting a distinguisher along an equality of coin polynomials -/

/-- **Transport of a distinguisher along `A.coins = B.coins`**: if the activations of `A` on
`X s` and of `B` on `Y s` agree for every seed `s` and every coin string, then the acceptance
probabilities of `A` on `X` and of `B` on `Y` agree. The coin types `A.Coins n` and
`B.Coins n` are identified by `finCongr` (`List.ofFn_congr`) and the seed spaces relabelled
by `uprob_comp_equiv`. This is the bridge by which a machine obtained from the closure
calculus (`Complexity.NUPPT.exists_comp`, `NUPPT.exists_withAdvice`) is compared with the
given adversary. -/
private theorem acceptProb_distinguisherL_congr {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] {A B : NUPPT}
    (hc : A.coins = B.coins) (n : ℕ) (X Y : σ → List Bool)
    (h : ∀ s r, A.runAtL n (X s) r = B.runAtL n (Y s) r) :
    acceptProb X (A.distinguisherL n) = acceptProb Y (B.distinguisherL n) := by
  have hlen : A.coinLen n = B.coinLen n := by simp only [NUPPT.coinLen, hc]
  let e : A.Coins n ≃ B.Coins n := Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr hlen) (Equiv.refl Bool)
  have hofn : ∀ r : A.Coins n, List.ofFn (e r) = List.ofFn r := fun r =>
    (List.ofFn_congr hlen r).symm
  unfold acceptProb
  have := uprob_comp_equiv ((Equiv.refl σ).prodCongr e)
    (fun z : σ × B.Coins n => B.distinguisherL n (Y z.1) z.2 = true)
  rw [← this]
  congr 1
  funext z
  simp only [Equiv.prodCongr_apply, Prod.map_fst, Prod.map_snd, Equiv.refl_apply,
    NUPPT.distinguisherL, NUPPT.runAt_eq, h, hofn]

/-! ### Efficient private-key encryption [PS10, Definition 24.7] -/

/-- An **efficient private-key encryption scheme** [PS10, Definition 24.7]: three PPTs
(`Complexity.NUPPT`s with empty advice) — `Gen(1^n)` samples a key `k`, `Enc_k(m)` encrypts
an `n`-bit message, `Dec_k(c)` decrypts a ciphertext into an `n`-bit message or `⊥` — such
that for every `n`, every `m ∈ {0,1}^n` and every choice of coins,
`Dec_k(Enc_k(m)) = m` where `k ← Gen(1^n)` (clause (4), probability one).
`Enc` and `Dec` are activated at parameter `n` on the pair `⟨k, m⟩` resp. `⟨k, c⟩`; the
output of `Dec` is decoded as an `n`-bit string by `decodeFin` (`none` is `⊥`).

**Deviation:** `PrivateKeyScheme`: messages at parameter `n` are the `n`-bit strings, keys
and ciphertexts arbitrary strings; `Enc` and `Dec` are activated at parameter `n` on
`⟨1^n, ⟨k, ·⟩⟩`; correctness holds for every coin string (the probability-one reading of
[PS10, Definition 24.6], `Complexity.NUPPT.computes_iff_uprob`); `Dec`'s `⊥` is any output
that does not decode to an `n`-bit string. -/
structure PrivateKeyScheme where
  /-- The key generator `Gen(1^n)`. -/
  gen : NUPPT
  /-- The encryption algorithm `Enc_k(m)`, activated on `⟨k, m⟩`. -/
  enc : NUPPT
  /-- The decryption algorithm `Dec_k(c)`, activated on `⟨k, c⟩`. -/
  dec : NUPPT
  /-- `Gen` is a PPT (no advice). -/
  gen_uniform : gen.Uniform
  /-- `Enc` is a PPT (no advice). -/
  enc_uniform : enc.Uniform
  /-- `Dec` is a PPT (no advice). -/
  dec_uniform : dec.Uniform
  /-- Perfect correctness [PS10, Definition 24.7 (4)], for every coin string. -/
  correct : ∀ n (m : Fin n → Bool) (rg : gen.Coins n) (re : enc.Coins n) (rd : dec.Coins n),
    decodeFin n (dec.runAt n (pairEncode (gen.runAt n [] rg)
      (enc.runAt n (pairEncode (gen.runAt n [] rg) (List.ofFn m)) re)) rd) = some m

namespace PrivateKeyScheme

/-- The ciphertext distribution `{k ← Gen(1^n) : Enc_k(m)}` of [PS10, Definition 91.1] as a
sampler from the coins of `Gen` and `Enc`. -/
def encDist (S : PrivateKeyScheme) (n : ℕ) (m : Fin n → Bool) :
    S.gen.Coins n × S.enc.Coins n → List Bool :=
  fun r => S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] r.1) (List.ofFn m)) r.2

/-- **Single-message security** [PS10, Definition 91.1]: for every non-uniform PPT `D` there
is a negligible `ε` such that for all `n` and all `m₀, m₁ ∈ {0,1}^n`, `D` distinguishes
`{k ← Gen(1^n) : Enc_k(m₀)}` from `{k ← Gen(1^n) : Enc_k(m₁)}` with advantage at most
`ε(n)`. The quantifier order (`ε` before `m₀, m₁`) is the text's.

**Deviation:** the distinguisher receives `1^n` with the ciphertext (D5); the bound is
`≤ ε(n)`. -/
def SingleMessageSecure (S : PrivateKeyScheme) : Prop :=
  ∀ D : NUPPT, ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, Negligible ε ∧ ∀ n (m₀ m₁ : Fin n → Bool),
    distAdv (S.encDist n m₀) (S.encDist n m₁) (D.distinguisherL n) ≤ ε n

/-- The encoding of a list of strings as a nested pair `⟨c₀, ⟨c₁, ⟨…, []⟩⟩⟩` (the tuple of
ciphertexts of [PS10, Definition 93.1]). -/
def encodeList : List (List Bool) → List Bool
  | [] => []
  | m :: ms => pairEncode m (encodeList ms)

/-- The distribution `{k ← Gen(1^n) : Enc_k(m₀), …, Enc_k(m_q)}` of [PS10, Definition 93.1]:
`q + 1` encryptions under one key with independent encryption coins, encoded by
`encodeList`. -/
def multiEncDist (S : PrivateKeyScheme) (n : ℕ) (q : ℕ) (m : Fin (q + 1) → Fin n → Bool) :
    S.gen.Coins n × (Fin (q + 1) → S.enc.Coins n) → List Bool :=
  fun r => encodeList (List.ofFn fun i =>
    S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] r.1) (List.ofFn (m i))) (r.2 i))

/-- **Multi-message security** [PS10, Definition 93.1]: for every non-uniform PPT `D` and
every polynomial `q` there is a negligible `ε` such that for all `n` and all message vectors
`m, m' ∈ ({0,1}^n)^{q(n)+1}`, `D` distinguishes the encryptions of `m` from those of `m'`
under one key `k ← Gen(1^n)` with advantage at most `ε(n)`. The count is `q(n) + 1`
messages (indices `0, …, q(n)`), as in the text.

**Deviation:** `D` receives `1^n`; the `q(n) + 1` ciphertexts are encoded by `encodeList`. -/
def MultiMessageSecure (S : PrivateKeyScheme) : Prop :=
  ∀ (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr), ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, Negligible ε ∧
    ∀ n (m m' : Fin (q.eval n + 1) → Fin n → Bool),
      distAdv (S.multiEncDist n (q.eval n) m) (S.multiEncDist n (q.eval n) m') (D.distinguisherL n) ≤ ε n

/-- **Deterministic encryption**: the output of `Enc` at every parameter and on every input
does not depend on its coins (the hypothesis of [PS10, Theorem 94.2]; statelessness is built
into the model, an `NUPPT` keeping no state between activations). -/
def Deterministic (S : PrivateKeyScheme) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (y : List Bool) (r r' : S.enc.Coins n), S.enc.runAt n y r = S.enc.runAt n y r'

/-- Unfolding of the ciphertext sampler. -/
theorem encDist_apply (S : PrivateKeyScheme) (n : ℕ) (m : Fin n → Bool)
    (r : S.gen.Coins n × S.enc.Coins n) :
    S.encDist n m r = S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] r.1) (List.ofFn m)) r.2 := rfl

/-- Unfolding of the list encoding on a cons. -/
theorem encodeList_cons (m : List Bool) (ms : List (List Bool)) :
    encodeList (m :: ms) = pairEncode m (encodeList ms) := rfl

/-- Unfolding of the list encoding on the empty list: `encodeList [] = []`. -/
theorem encodeList_nil : encodeList [] = [] := rfl

/-- Unfolding of the multi-message ciphertext sampler: the `encodeList` of the `q + 1`
encryptions `Enc(1^n, ⟨k, m_i⟩; s_i)` under the key `k = Gen(1^n; r.1)`, `s_i = r.2 i`. -/
theorem multiEncDist_apply (S : PrivateKeyScheme) (n q : ℕ) (m : Fin (q + 1) → Fin n → Bool)
    (r : S.gen.Coins n × (Fin (q + 1) → S.enc.Coins n)) :
    S.multiEncDist n q m r = encodeList (List.ofFn fun i =>
      S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] r.1) (List.ofFn (m i))) (r.2 i)) := rfl

/-- The defining property of `MultiMessageSecure`: for every `D` and `q` some negligible `ε`
bounds `D`'s advantage between the encryptions of any two message vectors `m, m'` of
`q(n) + 1` messages under one key. -/
theorem multiMessageSecure_iff (S : PrivateKeyScheme) :
    S.MultiMessageSecure ↔ ∀ (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr), ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, Negligible ε ∧
      ∀ n (m m' : Fin (q.eval n + 1) → Fin n → Bool),
        distAdv (S.multiEncDist n (q.eval n) m) (S.multiEncDist n (q.eval n) m')
          (D.distinguisherL n) ≤ ε n := Iff.rfl

/-- The first two components of the encoding of a tuple with at least two entries. -/
theorem firstTwo_encodeList_ofFn {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 < k) (f : Fin k → List Bool) :
    pairFstD (encodeList (List.ofFn f)) = f ⟨0, by omega⟩ ∧
      pairFstD (pairSndD (encodeList (List.ofFn f))) = f ⟨1, hk⟩ := by
  obtain ⟨k', rfl⟩ : ∃ k', k = k' + 2 := ⟨k - 2, by omega⟩
  simp [List.ofFn_succ, encodeList]

/-- **Multi-message security implies single-message security** (the sanity direction of
[PS10, §3.7]: Definition 93.1 "extends" Definition 91.1, the case `q = 0` of one message).

**Proof sketch.** Given `D`, let `B` be the machine `NUPPT.exists_comp D` with
`pre := pairFstD` and `post := id`: `B(1^n, ⟨c, []⟩; r) = D(1^n, c; r)`. For `q := const 0`
the vector `fun _ => m` has `multiEncDist n 0 (fun _ => m) r = encodeList [Enc_k(m; r.2 0)]`
(`List.ofFn_succ`, `encodeList`), so `B.distinguisherL n` on it is `D.distinguisherL n` on
`encDist n m (r.1, r.2 0)` (`pairFstD_pairEncode`). The hypothesis at `B`, `const 0` gives a
negligible `ε`; at `n, m₀, m₁` the two advantages agree after relabelling the seeds by
`S.gen.Coins n × (Fin 1 → S.enc.Coins n) ≃ S.gen.Coins n × S.enc.Coins n`
(`Equiv.funUnique`, `acceptProb_comp_equiv`) and the coins by `B.coins = D.coins`
(`acceptProb_distinguisherL_congr`). -/
theorem MultiMessageSecure.singleMessageSecure {S : PrivateKeyScheme} (h : S.MultiMessageSecure) :
    S.SingleMessageSecure := by
  intro D
  obtain ⟨B, hBc, -, -, hB⟩ := D.exists_comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD polyTimeComputable_id
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hD⟩ := h B (.const 0)
  refine ⟨ε, hε, fun n m₀ m₁ => ?_⟩
  -- the verdict of `B` on the one-ciphertext vector is the verdict of `D` on the ciphertext
  have key : ∀ m : Fin n → Bool,
      acceptProb (S.multiEncDist n ((PolyExpr.const 0).eval n) (fun _ => m)) (B.distinguisherL n) =
        acceptProb (S.encDist n m) (D.distinguisherL n) := by
    intro m
    have h1 := acceptProb_distinguisherL_congr hBc n
      (S.multiEncDist n ((PolyExpr.const 0).eval n) (fun _ => m))
      (fun r => S.encDist n m (r.1, r.2 0)) (fun r c => by
        have e : pairFstD (S.multiEncDist n ((PolyExpr.const 0).eval n) (fun _ => m) r) =
            S.encDist n m (r.1, r.2 0) := by
          simp [multiEncDist, encDist, encodeList, List.ofFn_succ]
        rw [hB, e]
        rfl)
    rw [h1]
    exact acceptProb_comp_equiv
      ((Equiv.refl (S.gen.Coins n)).prodCongr
        (@Equiv.funUnique (Fin ((PolyExpr.const 0).eval n + 1)) (S.enc.Coins n)
          (inferInstanceAs (Unique (Fin 1)))))
      (S.encDist n m) (D.distinguisherL n)
  have := hD n (fun _ => m₀) (fun _ => m₁)
  unfold distAdv at this ⊢
  rwa [key m₀, key m₁] at this

end PrivateKeyScheme

/-! ### The one-time pad with a truncated pad (Claim-92.a) -/

/-- The **truncated one-time pad**: the `n`-bit message `m` masked by the first `n` bits of
the `L`-bit pad `p` (`n ≤ L`), `(m ⊕ p|_n)_i = m_i ⊕ p_i`. With `L = n` this is the one-time
pad; with `p = G(k)` it is the encryption of [PS10, Algorithm 92.1]. -/
def padXor {n L : ℕ} (h : n ≤ L) (m : Fin n → Bool) (p : Fin L → Bool) : Fin n → Bool :=
  fun i => xor (m i) (p (Fin.castLE h i))

/-- The string form of the truncated pad: `List.zipWith xor` of the two encodings (which
truncates to the shorter list) is the encoding of `padXor`. -/
theorem zipWith_xor_ofFn {n L : ℕ} (h : n ≤ L) (m : Fin n → Bool) (p : Fin L → Bool) :
    List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn m) (List.ofFn p) = List.ofFn (padXor h m p) := by
  refine List.ext_getElem (by simp [Nat.min_eq_left h]) fun i h₁ h₂ => ?_
  simp [padXor, Fin.castLE]

/-- **Perfect secrecy of the one-time pad** (Claim-92.a, used in [PS10, Theorems 92.2 and
99.2]): for a uniform pad `p ← U_L` the distributions `m₀ ⊕ p|_n` and `m₁ ⊕ p|_n` are
identical, so every distinguisher accepts them with the same probability.

**Proof sketch.** The map `p ↦ p ⊕ d`, where `d` extends `m₀ ⊕ m₁` by zeros to `L` bits, is
an involution of the pad space with `m₁ ⊕ (p ⊕ d)|_n = m₀ ⊕ p|_n`; relabelling the uniform
pad by it (`acceptProb_comp_equiv`) proves the claim. -/
theorem acceptProb_padXor {ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ] {n L : ℕ} (h : n ≤ L) (m₀ m₁ : Fin n → Bool)
    (D : (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun p : Fin L → Bool => padXor h m₀ p) D =
      acceptProb (fun p : Fin L → Bool => padXor h m₁ p) D := by
  let d : Fin L → Bool := fun j =>
    if hj : j.val < n then xor (m₀ ⟨j, hj⟩) (m₁ ⟨j, hj⟩) else false
  have hinv : Function.Involutive (fun p : Fin L → Bool => fun j => xor (p j) (d j)) := by
    intro p
    funext j
    show xor (xor (p j) (d j)) (d j) = p j
    cases p j <;> cases d j <;> rfl
  have key : ∀ p : Fin L → Bool, padXor h m₁ (fun j => xor (p j) (d j)) = padXor h m₀ p := by
    intro p
    funext i
    simp only [padXor, d, Fin.coe_castLE, i.isLt, dite_true, Fin.eta]
    cases m₀ i <;> cases m₁ i <;> cases p (Fin.castLE h i) <;> rfl
  calc acceptProb (fun p : Fin L → Bool => padXor h m₀ p) D
      = acceptProb (fun p : Fin L → Bool => padXor h m₁ (hinv.toPerm _ p)) D := by
        congr 1
        funext p
        exact (key p).symm
    _ = acceptProb (fun p : Fin L → Bool => padXor h m₁ p) D :=
        acceptProb_comp_equiv (hinv.toPerm _) (fun p => padXor h m₁ p) D

/-- **The four-hybrid bound of [PS10, Theorem 92.2], concrete:** for a generator
`G : σ → {0,1}^L`, messages `m₀, m₁ ∈ {0,1}^n` (`n ≤ L`) and any distinguisher `D`, the
advantage of `D` between `m₀ ⊕ G(s)|_n` and `m₁ ⊕ G(s)|_n` (`s` uniform) is at most
`prgAdv G (D ∘ (m₀ ⊕ ·)) + prgAdv G (D ∘ (m₁ ⊕ ·))`.

**Proof sketch.** Hybrids `H¹ = m₀ ⊕ G(U)`, `H² = m₀ ⊕ U_L`, `H³ = m₁ ⊕ U_L`, `H⁴ = m₁ ⊕ G(U)`:
`|P(H¹) − P(H²)| = prgAdv G (D ∘ (m₀ ⊕ ·))` and `|P(H³) − P(H⁴)| = prgAdv G (D ∘ (m₁ ⊕ ·))`
are the definitions of `prgAdv` and `distAdv` (the sunglass identity `distAdv_comp`, here
definitional), `P(H²) = P(H³)` is `acceptProb_padXor`, and the triangle inequality
`abs_sub_le` finishes. (The text's "three gaps, `1/(3p(n))`" is this two-term bound.) -/
theorem distAdv_padXor_le {σ ρ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype ρ] {n L : ℕ} (h : n ≤ L)
    (G : σ → Fin L → Bool) (m₀ m₁ : Fin n → Bool) (D : (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv (fun s => padXor h m₀ (G s)) (fun s => padXor h m₁ (G s)) D ≤
      prgAdv G (fun t r => D (padXor h m₀ t) r) + prgAdv G (fun t r => D (padXor h m₁ t) r) := by
  have e := acceptProb_padXor h m₀ m₁ D
  change |acceptProb (fun s => padXor h m₀ (G s)) D - acceptProb (fun s => padXor h m₁ (G s)) D| ≤
    |acceptProb (fun s => padXor h m₀ (G s)) D - acceptProb (fun p => padXor h m₀ p) D| +
    |acceptProb (fun s => padXor h m₁ (G s)) D - acceptProb (fun p => padXor h m₁ p) D|
  rw [← e, abs_sub_comm (acceptProb (fun s => padXor h m₁ (G s)) D)]
  exact abs_sub_le _ _ _

/-! ### The scheme of [PS10, Algorithm 92.1] -/

/-- The raw string function of `Enc` and `Dec` of [PS10, Algorithm 92.1]: on the machine
layout `⟨⟨⟨1^n, ⟨k, w⟩⟩, α⟩, r⟩` output `w ⊕ F(k)` (bitwise, truncated to the shorter string),
where `F` evaluates the generator. -/
def prgPadFun (F : List Bool → List Bool) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  List.zipWith xor (pairSndD (NUPPT.inArg z)) (F (pairFstD (NUPPT.inArg z)))

/-- `prgPadFun F` is polynomial-time when `F` is: one evaluation of `F` and one bitwise
exclusive-or (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairXor`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_prgPadFun {F : List Bool → List Bool} (hF : PolyTimeComputable F) :
    PolyTimeComputable (prgPadFun F) := by
  have h := polyTimeComputable_pairXor.comp
    ((polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inArg).pairEncode
      (hF.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inArg)))
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  simp [prgPadFun, Function.comp]

/-- The activation of the pad machine on `⟨k, w⟩` is `w ⊕ F(k)`. -/
theorem runAt_prgPad {F : List Bool → List Bool} (hF : PolyTimeComputable F) (coins : PolyExpr)
    (n : ℕ) (k w : List Bool)
    (r : (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform (polyTimeComputable_prgPadFun hF) coins).Coins n) :
    (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform (polyTimeComputable_prgPadFun hF) coins).runAt n (pairEncode k w) r =
      List.zipWith xor w (F k) := by
  rw [NUPPT.runAt_eq, NUPPT.runAtL_ofPolyTimeUniform]
  simp [prgPadFun, NUPPT.inArg, NUPPT.advInput]

/-- The activation of the key generator (the coin string is the key). -/
theorem runAt_coinKey (coins : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ)
    (r : (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_pairSndD coins).Coins n) :
    (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_pairSndD coins).runAt n [] r = List.ofFn r := by
  rw [NUPPT.runAt_eq, NUPPT.runAtL_ofPolyTimeUniform]
  simp

/-- Masking twice with the same pad (at least as long as the message) is the identity. -/
private theorem zipWith_xor_xor_self : ∀ (m p : List Bool), m.length ≤ p.length →
    List.zipWith xor (List.zipWith xor m p) p = m
  | [], _, _ => by simp
  | _ :: _, [], h => by simp at h
  | a :: m, b :: p, h => by
    simp only [List.zipWith_cons_cons, List.cons.injEq]
    exact ⟨by cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl, zipWith_xor_xor_self m p (by simpa using h)⟩

/-- **The encryption scheme of [PS10, Algorithm 92.1]** for a generator `G` with evaluator
`F`: `Gen(1^n)` outputs a uniform `n`-bit seed `k` (its coin string), `Enc_k(m) = m ⊕ G(k)|_n`
and `Dec_k(c) = c ⊕ G(k)|_n` (`Enc` and `Dec` are deterministic, coins `const 0`). Correctness
is `(m ⊕ p) ⊕ p = m` for a pad `p = G(k)` of length `ℓ(n) > n`.

**Deviation:** the key is an `n`-bit seed and the pad is the first `n` bits of `G(k)` (the
text's `n/2`-bit key for a length-doubling `G` requires `n` even; with syntactic polynomial
lengths (D9) a key length that is a non-constant function of the message length is never
shorter than the message, so the "short key" economy of §3.6 is a matter of parametrization
and the security argument is unchanged); the evaluator `F` of `G` is an explicit argument
rather than extracted from `PRG.Easy`. -/
noncomputable def prgScheme (P : PRG) (F : List Bool → List Bool) (hF : PolyTimeComputable F)
    (hG : ∀ n (s : Fin n → Bool), F (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (P.G n s)) : PrivateKeyScheme where
  gen := NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_pairSndD .var
  enc := NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform (polyTimeComputable_prgPadFun hF) (.const 0)
  dec := NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform (polyTimeComputable_prgPadFun hF) (.const 0)
  gen_uniform := NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform_uniform _ _
  enc_uniform := NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform_uniform _ _
  dec_uniform := NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform_uniform _ _
  correct := by
    intro n m rg re rd
    rw [runAt_coinKey, runAt_prgPad hF, runAt_prgPad hF, hG, zipWith_xor_xor_self, decodeFin_ofFn]
    simp only [List.length_ofFn]
    exact (P.expands n).le

/-- **The ciphertext distribution of Algorithm 92.1** is `m ⊕ G(k)|_n` for a uniform seed `k`
(the encryption coins are unused): `encDist n m (k, _) = ofFn (padXor m (G n k))`. -/
theorem prgScheme_encDist (P : PRG) (F : List Bool → List Bool) (hF : PolyTimeComputable F)
    (hG : ∀ n (s : Fin n → Bool), F (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (P.G n s)) (n : ℕ)
    (m : Fin n → Bool) (r : (prgScheme P F hF hG).gen.Coins n × (prgScheme P F hF hG).enc.Coins n) :
    (prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n m r = List.ofFn (padXor (P.expands n).le m (P.G n r.1)) := by
  show (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform (polyTimeComputable_prgPadFun hF) (.const 0)).runAt n
    (pairEncode ((NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_pairSndD .var).runAt n [] r.1)
      (List.ofFn m)) r.2 = _
  rw [runAt_coinKey, runAt_prgPad hF, hG]
  exact zipWith_xor_ofFn (P.expands n).le m (P.G n r.1)

/-- **Dropping the unused encryption coins of Algorithm 92.1**: the probability that a
distinguisher accepts a ciphertext `encDist n m` of `prgScheme` is the probability that it
accepts the string of `m ⊕ G(s)|_n` for a uniform seed `s`. The seed relabelling
`(s, r) ↦ ((s, ∅), r)` is a bijection because the encryption coin type `Fin 0 → Bool` is a
singleton (`Fin.elim0`); the ciphertext is `prgScheme_encDist`. -/
private theorem acceptProb_prgScheme_encDist (P : PRG) (F : List Bool → List Bool)
    (hF : PolyTimeComputable F) (hG : ∀ n (s : Fin n → Bool), F (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (P.G n s))
    (n : ℕ) (m : Fin n → Bool) {ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ] (Dst : List Bool → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb ((prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n m) Dst =
      acceptProb (fun s : Fin n → Bool => padXor (P.expands n).le m (P.G n s))
        (fun t r => Dst (List.ofFn t) r) := by
  let e : (Fin n → Bool) × ρ ≃
      ((prgScheme P F hF hG).gen.Coins n × (prgScheme P F hF hG).enc.Coins n) × ρ :=
    { toFun := fun z => ((z.1, fun i => Fin.elim0 i), z.2)
      invFun := fun z => (z.1.1, z.2)
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl
      right_inv := fun _ => Prod.ext (Prod.ext rfl (funext fun i => Fin.elim0 i)) rfl }
  unfold acceptProb
  rw [← uprob_comp_equiv e]
  congr 1
  funext z
  simp only [e, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, prgScheme_encDist]

/-- **A machine that runs `D` on `m ⊕ t` is the distinguisher `D ∘ (m ⊕ ·)`**: if
`B(1^n, t; r) = D(1^n, m ⊕ t|_n; r)` for every `L`-bit string `t` (with `B.coins = D.coins`),
then the PRG advantage of `B` as a typed distinguisher of `L`-bit strings equals the PRG
advantage of `D ∘ (m ⊕ ·)` — the machine form of the hybrid distinguishers of
[PS10, Theorem 92.2, proof] (`acceptProb_distinguisherL_congr` on both terms of `prgAdv`). -/
private theorem prgAdv_eq_of_runAtL {n L : ℕ} (h : n ≤ L) {B D : NUPPT} (hc : B.coins = D.coins)
    (m : Fin n → Bool) {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (G : σ → Fin L → Bool)
    (hB : ∀ (t : Fin L → Bool) r,
      B.runAtL n (List.ofFn t) r = D.runAtL n (List.ofFn (padXor h m t)) r) :
    prgAdv G (fun t r => D.distinguisherL n (List.ofFn (padXor h m t)) r) =
      prgAdv G (B.distinguisher n L) := by
  unfold prgAdv distAdv
  have e₁ : acceptProb G (B.distinguisher n L) =
      acceptProb (fun s => List.ofFn (G s)) (B.distinguisherL n) := rfl
  have e₂ : acceptProb id (B.distinguisher n L) =
      acceptProb (fun t : Fin L → Bool => List.ofFn t) (B.distinguisherL n) := rfl
  rw [e₁, e₂,
    acceptProb_distinguisherL_congr hc n _ (fun s => List.ofFn (padXor h m (G s)))
      (fun s r => hB (G s) r),
    acceptProb_distinguisherL_congr hc n _ (fun t => List.ofFn (padXor h m t)) (fun t r => hB t r)]
  rfl

/-- **[PS10, Theorem 92.2]: the scheme of Algorithm 92.1 is single-message secure** when `G`
is a pseudorandom generator.

**Proof sketch.** Fix a non-uniform PPT `D`. At each `n` choose a pair `(m₀ⁿ, m₁ⁿ)`
maximizing `distAdv (encDist n m₀) (encDist n m₁) (D.distinguisherL n)` over the finite
message space (`Finset.exists_max_image`; the text's footnote: "`Mᵢ` is non-uniform as it has
the message hard-coded"). Concrete step: by `prgScheme_encDist` the sampler `encDist n mᵢ`
is `(k, _) ↦ ofFn (padXor mᵢ (G n k))`; drop the unused encryption coins (the coin type
`Fin 0 → Bool` is a singleton) and move `List.ofFn` into the distinguisher
(`acceptProb_prgScheme_encDist`), and apply `distAdv_padXor_le`: the advantage at `n` is at most
`prgAdv (G n) D₀ⁿ + prgAdv (G n) D₁ⁿ` with `Dᵢⁿ t r := D.distinguisherL n (ofFn (padXor mᵢⁿ t)) r`
— the four hybrids `H¹ = m₀ ⊕ G(U_n)`, `H² = m₀ ⊕ U_ℓ`, `H³ = m₁ ⊕ U_ℓ`, `H⁴ = m₁ ⊕ G(U_n)` of
the text. Machine step: for `i = 0, 1` the machine `Bᵢ` has advice `⟨ofFn mᵢⁿ, D.advice n⟩`
(`NUPPT.exists_withAdvice` with the bound `var`), coins `D.coins`, and on `⟨1^n, t⟩` computes
`zipWith xor (ofFn mᵢⁿ) t` (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairXor`; equal to
`ofFn (padXor mᵢⁿ t)` by `zipWith_xor_ofFn`) and runs `D` on it (`NUPPT.exists_comp`), so
`prgAdv (G n) Dᵢⁿ = prgAdv (G n) (Bᵢ.distinguisher n (ℓ n))` after transporting the coins
along `Bᵢ.coins = D.coins` (`prgAdv_eq_of_runAtL`, `acceptProb_distinguisherL_congr`).
Asymptotic step:
`ν n := prgAdv (G n) (B₀.distinguisher n (ℓ n)) + prgAdv (G n) (B₁.distinguisher n (ℓ n))` is
negligible by `PRG.secure_iff` applied to `hP` and `Negligible.add`; by maximality
`distAdv (encDist n m₀) (encDist n m₁) (D.distinguisherL n) ≤ ν n` for every `n, m₀, m₁`, so
`ε := ν` witnesses `SingleMessageSecure`. -/
theorem prgScheme_singleMessageSecure (P : PRG) (hP : P.Secure) (F : List Bool → List Bool)
    (hF : PolyTimeComputable F) (hG : ∀ n (s : Fin n → Bool), F (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (P.G n s)) :
    (prgScheme P F hF hG).SingleMessageSecure := by
  intro D
  -- the worst message pair at each parameter (hard-wired into the reductions)
  have hmax : ∀ n, ∃ p : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool), ∀ q : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool),
      distAdv ((prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n q.1) ((prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n q.2)
          (D.distinguisherL n) ≤
        distAdv ((prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n p.1) ((prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n p.2)
          (D.distinguisherL n) := by
    intro n
    obtain ⟨p, -, hp⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image Finset.univ
      (fun q : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) =>
        distAdv ((prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n q.1) ((prgScheme P F hF hG).encDist n q.2)
          (D.distinguisherL n)) Finset.univ_nonempty
    exact ⟨p, fun q => hp q (Finset.mem_univ q)⟩
  choose μ hμ using hmax
  -- the reductions `Bᵢ`: mask the challenge with the hard-wired message, then run `D`
  have hpre : PolyTimeComputable fun z => List.zipWith xor (pairSndD z) (pairFstD z) := by
    have := polyTimeComputable_pairXor.comp
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)
    convert this using 1
    funext z
    simp [Function.comp]
  obtain ⟨D', hD'c, -, -, hD'⟩ := D.exists_comp hpre polyTimeComputable_id
  obtain ⟨B₀, hB₀c, hB₀⟩ := D'.exists_withAdvice (fun n => List.ofFn (μ n).1) .var (fun n => by simp)
  obtain ⟨B₁, hB₁c, hB₁⟩ := D'.exists_withAdvice (fun n => List.ofFn (μ n).2) .var (fun n => by simp)
  have hrun : ∀ (B : NUPPT) (β : ∀ n, Fin n → Bool),
      (∀ n y r, B.runAtL n y r = D'.runAtL n (pairEncode y (List.ofFn (β n))) r) →
      ∀ n (t : Fin (P.stretch.eval n) → Bool) r,
        B.runAtL n (List.ofFn t) r = D.runAtL n (List.ofFn (padXor (P.expands n).le (β n) t)) r := by
    intro B β hB n t r
    rw [hB, hD', pairSndD_pairEncode, pairFstD_pairEncode, zipWith_xor_ofFn]
    rfl
  -- the negligible bound: the two PRG advantages of `B₀`, `B₁`
  refine ⟨fun n => prgAdv (P.G n) (B₀.distinguisher n (P.stretch.eval n)) +
    prgAdv (P.G n) (B₁.distinguisher n (P.stretch.eval n)), (hP.2 B₀).add (hP.2 B₁),
    fun n m₀ m₁ => ?_⟩
  refine (hμ n (m₀, m₁)).trans ?_
  unfold distAdv
  dsimp only
  rw [acceptProb_prgScheme_encDist, acceptProb_prgScheme_encDist,
    ← prgAdv_eq_of_runAtL (P.expands n).le (hB₀c.trans hD'c) (μ n).1 (P.G n) (hrun B₀ _ hB₀ n),
    ← prgAdv_eq_of_runAtL (P.expands n).le (hB₁c.trans hD'c) (μ n).2 (P.G n) (hrun B₁ _ hB₁ n)]
  exact distAdv_padXor_le (P.expands n).le (P.G n) (μ n).1 (μ n).2
    (fun t r => D.distinguisherL n (List.ofFn t) r)

/-! ### Deterministic schemes are not multi-message secure [PS10, Theorem 94.2] -/

namespace PrivateKeyScheme

/-- The raw string function of the distinguisher of [PS10, Theorem 94.2]: on the layout
`⟨⟨⟨1^n, w⟩, α⟩, r⟩` with `w = ⟨c₀, ⟨c₁, …⟩⟩`, output `[c₀ = c₁]`. -/
def firstTwoEqFun (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  [decide (pairFstD (NUPPT.inArg z) = pairFstD (pairSndD (NUPPT.inArg z)))]

/-- `firstTwoEqFun` is polynomial-time: two projections and one string equality test
(`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairEq`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun : PolyTimeComputable firstTwoEqFun := by
  have h := polyTimeComputable_pairEq.comp
    ((polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inArg).pairEncode
      ((polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD).comp
        NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inArg))
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  simp [firstTwoEqFun, Function.comp]

/-- The distinguisher `[c₀ = c₁]` accepts a word `w` iff its first two components agree. -/
theorem distinguisherL_firstTwoEq (coins : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool)
    (r : (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun coins).Coins n) :
    (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun coins).distinguisherL n w r = true ↔
      pairFstD w = pairFstD (pairSndD w) := by
  rw [NUPPT.distinguisherL, NUPPT.runAt_eq, NUPPT.runAtL_ofPolyTimeUniform]
  simp [firstTwoEqFun, NUPPT.inArg, NUPPT.advInput]

/-- **[PS10, Theorem 94.2]: a deterministic (stateless) encryption scheme is not
multi-message secure.** The text's argument: for messages `m₀ ≠ m₁`, the encryptions
`(c₀, c₁)` of `(m₀, m₀)` satisfy `c₀ = c₁` when `Enc` is deterministic, while the encryptions
`(c'₀, c'₁)` of `(m₀, m₁)` satisfy `c'₀ ≠ c'₁` (otherwise `Dec_k` would recover both `m₀` and
`m₁` from the same ciphertext, contradicting correctness); the PPT distinguisher `[c₀ = c₁]`
(`firstTwoEqFun`, with `q := const 1`, two messages) therefore has advantage exactly `1` at
every `n ≥ 1`, which no negligible `ε` bounds.

**Deviation:** the proof uses correctness (to get `c'₀ ≠ c'₁`) and `n ≥ 1` (two distinct
messages), both implicit in the text; "stateless" is built into the model.

**Proof sketch.** Assume multi-message security and apply it to the machine
`ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun` (no coins) and `q := const 1`, obtaining
a negligible `ε`; pick `n := n₀ + 1` with `|ε n| < 1` (the case `c = 1` of negligibility).
With `m₀ := 0^n`, `m₁ := 1^n` (distinct at index `0`), compare the vectors `v = (m₀, m₀)` and
`v' = (m₀, m₁)`. The verdict of the machine on `multiEncDist n 1 w r` is the equality of the
first two ciphertexts (`distinguisherL_firstTwoEq`, `firstTwo_encodeList_ofFn`). On `v` the
two ciphertexts are the same deterministic function of `(k, m₀)` (`hS`), so the acceptance
probability is `1` (`uprob_true`); on `v'` equal ciphertexts would give
`some m₀ = Dec_k(c'₀) = Dec_k(c'₁) = some m₁` by `S.correct`, so the acceptance probability is
`0` (`uprob_false`). Hence `distAdv = 1 ≤ ε n`, contradicting `|ε n| < 1`. -/
theorem not_multiMessageSecure_of_deterministic (S : PrivateKeyScheme) (hS : S.Deterministic) :
    ¬ S.MultiMessageSecure := by
  intro hsec
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hD⟩ :=
    hsec (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun (.const 0)) (.const 1)
  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ := hε 1
  -- the parameter `n = n₀ + 1 ≥ 1` at which `ε n < 1`
  have hεn : |ε (n₀ + 1)| < 1 := by
    have h := hn₀ (n₀ + 1) (Nat.le_succ n₀)
    have h1 : (1 : ℝ) / ((n₀ + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 1 ≤ 1 := by
      rw [pow_one]
      exact div_le_one_of_le₀ (by exact_mod_cast Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n₀))
        (by positivity)
    linarith
  -- two distinct messages and the two message vectors `(m₀, m₀)` and `(m₀, m₁)`
  set n := n₀ + 1 with hn
  let m₀ : Fin n → Bool := fun _ => false
  let m₁ : Fin n → Bool := fun _ => true
  have hm : m₀ ≠ m₁ := fun h => by
    have := congrFun h ⟨0, by omega⟩
    simp [m₀, m₁] at this
  have h0 : 0 < (PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1 := Nat.succ_pos _
  have h1 : 1 < (PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1 := by simp
  let v : Fin ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1) → Fin n → Bool := fun _ => m₀
  let v' : Fin ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1) → Fin n → Bool :=
    fun i => if i.val = 0 then m₀ else m₁
  have hadv := hD n v v'
  -- the verdict on a two-message encryption is the equality of the two ciphertexts
  have hacc : ∀ w : Fin ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1) → Fin n → Bool,
      acceptProb (S.multiEncDist n ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n) w)
        ((NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun (.const 0)).distinguisherL n) =
      uprob fun z : (S.gen.Coins n × (Fin ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1) → S.enc.Coins n)) ×
          (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun (.const 0)).Coins n =>
        S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] z.1.1) (List.ofFn (w ⟨0, h0⟩))) (z.1.2 ⟨0, h0⟩) =
          S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] z.1.1) (List.ofFn (w ⟨1, h1⟩)))
            (z.1.2 ⟨1, h1⟩) := by
    intro w
    unfold acceptProb
    congr 1
    funext z
    rw [distinguisherL_firstTwoEq, multiEncDist]
    obtain ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ := firstTwo_encodeList_ofFn h1 fun i =>
      S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] z.1.1) (List.ofFn (w i))) (z.1.2 i)
    rw [h₁, h₂]
  -- on `(m₀, m₀)` the two ciphertexts agree: acceptance probability `1`
  have hone : acceptProb (S.multiEncDist n ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n) v)
      ((NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun (.const 0)).distinguisherL n) = 1 := by
    rw [hacc]
    have : (fun z : (S.gen.Coins n × (Fin ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1) → S.enc.Coins n)) ×
          (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun (.const 0)).Coins n =>
        S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] z.1.1) (List.ofFn (v ⟨0, h0⟩))) (z.1.2 ⟨0, h0⟩) =
          S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] z.1.1) (List.ofFn (v ⟨1, h1⟩)))
            (z.1.2 ⟨1, h1⟩)) = fun _ => True := by
      funext z
      exact propext ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => hS n _ _ _⟩
    rw [this, uprob_true]
  -- on `(m₀, m₁)` the two ciphertexts differ (by correctness): acceptance probability `0`
  have hzero : acceptProb (S.multiEncDist n ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n) v')
      ((NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun (.const 0)).distinguisherL n) = 0 := by
    rw [hacc]
    have : (fun z : (S.gen.Coins n × (Fin ((PolyExpr.const 1).eval n + 1) → S.enc.Coins n)) ×
          (NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_firstTwoEqFun (.const 0)).Coins n =>
        S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] z.1.1) (List.ofFn (v' ⟨0, h0⟩))) (z.1.2 ⟨0, h0⟩) =
          S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode (S.gen.runAt n [] z.1.1) (List.ofFn (v' ⟨1, h1⟩)))
            (z.1.2 ⟨1, h1⟩)) = fun _ => False := by
      funext z
      refine propext ⟨fun heq => ?_, fun h => h.elim⟩
      have hv0 : v' ⟨0, h0⟩ = m₀ := by simp [v']
      have hv1 : v' ⟨1, h1⟩ = m₁ := by simp [v']
      rw [hv0, hv1] at heq
      have c₀ := S.correct n m₀ z.1.1 (z.1.2 ⟨0, h0⟩) (fun _ => false)
      have c₁ := S.correct n m₁ z.1.1 (z.1.2 ⟨1, h1⟩) (fun _ => false)
      rw [heq, c₁, Option.some.injEq] at c₀
      exact hm c₀.symm
    rw [this, uprob_false]
  -- the advantage is `1`, but `ε n < 1`
  rw [distAdv, hone, hzero] at hadv
  have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ε n := by simpa using hadv
  linarith [le_abs_self (ε n)]

end PrivateKeyScheme

end TCSlib.Cryptography

-- finding 12). Drop it once that file imports `NonUniform` itself.
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.NonUniform
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Adversary
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.EnsemblesLemmas
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Sampling
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Negligible
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Indistinguishability
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.GeneratorFromPermutation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Ensembles and computational indistinguishability

The asymptotic notion of [PS10, §3.1]: *ensembles* of probability distributions over
`{0,1}^{ℓ(n)}` and *computational indistinguishability* `{X_n} ≈ {Y_n}` against non-uniform
PPT distinguishers, with the three properties the rest of chapters 3 and 4 use over and over:
closure under efficient operations (Lemma 71.5), the hybrid lemma (Lemma 71.6) and the
prediction lemma (Lemma 73.8).

Foundation decision D6: an ensemble is a family of samplers `X n : σ n → (Fin (ℓ n) → Bool)`
from arbitrary finite nonempty seed types (the uniform ensemble has seeds `Fin (ℓ n) → Bool`); every
length is a syntactic polynomial `Complexity.PolyExpr` (D9). "Efficiently samplable" is the
distribution-level predicate `Ensemble.Samplable`: a polynomial-time sampler from `s n`
uniform bits whose output law is exactly `X n` (`StatClose … 0`). The headline form of
Definition 69.4 gives the distinguisher the input `1^n` (`Ensemble.Indist`, D5); the literal
form `Ensemble.IndistLit` (the distinguisher receives the sample `t` only, activation at
parameter `|t| = ℓ n`) is stated next to it with the bridges `Indist.toLit` and
`IndistLit.toIndist` (injective, i.e. non-constant, `ℓ`; for constant `ℓ` the two forms
coincide as well, by point tests, which is not formalized), never unified silently.

Every asymptotic statement is proved by instantiating a concrete reduction of
`TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Indistinguishability` [Gar26, §3.2] at each `n`, exhibiting
the reduction as a `Complexity.NUPPT` by the closure catalogue of
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Closure`, and finishing with negligible-function arithmetic
(`not_negligible_iff`, the "infinitely many `n` with `1/p(n)`" idiom of the text,
`not_negligible_iff_exists_polyExpr`).

**Deviation:** `Ensemble`: dyadic samplable distributions; `Indist` gives `D` the input `1^n`
(literal form `IndistLit`, equivalent for every `PolyExpr ℓ`: proved for injective `ℓ`, the
constant case by point tests, not formalized).

The machine constructions and the probability bookkeeping behind the proofs (the negated,
padded-image and multicopy reductions as `NUPPT`s, coin-splitting bijections, the exactness
transfer `StatClose … 0` through `copies`) live in the sibling file
`TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.EnsemblesLemmas` (inner namespace `EnsembleLemmas`), which
exists only to keep this file within the repository's size limit.

**Repair (run-3 audit P2-2):** `Ensemble` carries the field `nonempty` (an empty seed type is
not a distribution), which restores the frozen shapes of `prediction_lemma` and
`Ensemble.NextBitUnpredictable.pseudorandom` (`NextBit.lean`); the nonemptiness instances
of `predict_eq` are discharged automatically for ensemble seeds and machine coins.

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble` — an ensemble over `{0,1}^{ℓ(n)}` [PS10, Definition 69.3];
  `Ensemble.uniform` — the uniform ensemble `{U_{ℓ(n)}}`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.Samplable` — efficiently samplable (distribution level, D6).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.Indist`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.IndistLit` —
  computational indistinguishability [PS10, Definition 69.4], headline and literal forms;
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Distinguishes`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.DistinguishesWith` —
  "`D` distinguishes with probability `ε` / `μ(·)`".
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.Pseudorandom` — indistinguishable from uniform
  [PS10, Definition 74.1].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.push` — the image ensemble `{M(X_n)}` under an `NUPPT`;
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.copies` — `t(n)` independent copies.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.mixEnsemble` — the sampler of `b ← {0,1}; t ← X^b_n` [PS10, Lemma 73.8].

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.Indist.refl`, `Indist.symm`, `Indist.trans` — `≈` is an
  equivalence relation (transitivity is the two-step hybrid lemma, [PS10, §3.1.1]).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.Indist.push` — closure under efficient operations
  [PS10, Lemma 71.5].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.hybrid_lemma` — the hybrid lemma [PS10, Lemma 71.6], concrete.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Ensemble.Indist.copies` — polynomially many copies (the multicopy
  corollary of the hybrid lemma, [Gar26, Lemma 3.3]).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.predict_eq` — predicting is distinguishing, the identity behind
  [PS10, p. 73 ("show this!") and Lemma 73.8].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.prediction_lemma` — the prediction lemma [PS10, Lemma 73.8].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.not_negligible_iff_exists_polyExpr` — "for infinitely many `n`,
  advantage `≥ 1/p(n)`" is non-negligibility [PS10, §3.1, the ubiquitous contradiction idiom].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.pairwise_sampling_ineq` — the pairwise-independent sampling
  inequality [PS10, Appendix A, p. 189].

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§3.1: Definitions 69.3, 69.4; §3.1.1: Lemmas 71.5, 71.6, 73.8; §3.2.1: Definition 74.1;
  Appendix A, p. 189.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.2 (Definition 3.4, Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3), Theorem 2.4.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Complexity Turing Finset

/-! ### Ensembles -/

/-- An **ensemble** of probability distributions over `{0,1}^{ℓ(n)}` [PS10, Definition 69.3]:
at each `n` a sampler `X n` from a finite seed type `σ n` (uniformly distributed seeds) into
the `ℓ(n)`-bit strings, the distribution `X_n` being the pushforward of the uniform seed. The
length `ℓ` is a syntactic polynomial (D9).

**Deviation:** each `X_n` is the pushforward of the uniform distribution on a finite nonempty
seed set, so its probabilities are rational (not necessarily dyadic: three seeds mapped to
distinct strings give masses `1/3`; every efficiently samplable ensemble, `Samplable`, has dyadic
laws, D6, but not every dyadic ensemble is samplable, e.g. the point mass at an uncomputable bit;
gate 03a, round 2, R2-3), and it lives
on strings of the fixed length `ℓ(n)` that Definition 69.4 requires (Definition 69.3 allows
arbitrary distributions over `{0,1}^*`). Every ensemble of chapters 3 and 4 is of this form;
the non-dyadic ideal distributions (primes, `Z_q`, permutations) appear only inside
experiments, approximated by the rejection samplers of `Asymptotic/Sampling.lean` (D6, D10).

**Repair (run-3 audit P2-2):** the field `nonempty` was added to the frozen structure of
DESIGN.md §2.11. An empty seed type is not a distribution (every event has probability `0`),
and without the field `NextBitUnpredictable` was vacuous for an empty-seed ensemble that is
not pseudorandom, so `prediction_lemma` and `NextBitUnpredictable.pseudorandom` needed ad hoc
nonemptiness hypotheses. Machine coin types `Fin k → Bool` and every seed type of the campaign
are nonempty, so constructions fill the field by instance resolution. -/
structure Ensemble (ℓ : PolyExpr) where
  /-- The seed type at parameter `n`. -/
  σ : ℕ → Type
  /-- Seed types are finite. -/
  [fintype : ∀ n, Fintype (σ n)]
  /-- Seed types are nonempty: the sampler defines a probability distribution. -/
  [nonempty : ∀ n, Nonempty (σ n)]
  /-- The sampler at parameter `n`. -/
  X : ∀ n, σ n → (Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool)

attribute [instance] Ensemble.fintype Ensemble.nonempty

namespace Ensemble

variable {ℓ : PolyExpr}

/-- The uniform ensemble `{U_{ℓ(n)}}` [PS10, §3.2.1]: seeds are the strings themselves. -/
def uniform (ℓ : PolyExpr) : Ensemble ℓ where
  σ n := Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool
  X _ := id

/-- Field equation of the uniform ensemble: the seed type at `n` is `{0,1}^{ℓ(n)}`. -/
theorem uniform_σ (ℓ : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) : (uniform ℓ).σ n = (Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool) := rfl

/-- Field equation of the uniform ensemble: the sampler at `n` is the identity on seeds, read
along `uniform_σ`. -/
theorem uniform_X (ℓ : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) (x : (uniform ℓ).σ n) :
    (uniform ℓ).X n x = cast (uniform_σ ℓ n) x := rfl

/-- **Efficiently samplable** ensemble (distribution level, D6): there is a syntactic
polynomial `s` and a polynomial-time sampler `S` such that at every `n` the law of
`S(⟨1^n, r⟩)` for `s(n)` uniform bits `r` (padded or truncated to `ℓ(n)` bits) is exactly the
law of `X n` (`StatClose … 0`). This is the "efficiently sample" of [PS10, p. 72, Example];
the multicopy lemma that assumes it is [Gar26, Lemma 3.3] (`Indist.copies`). -/
def Samplable (X : Ensemble ℓ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (s : PolyExpr) (S : List Bool → List Bool), PolyTimeComputable S ∧
    ∀ n, StatClose (fun r : Fin (s.eval n) → Bool =>
      padFin (ℓ.eval n) (S (NUPPT.advInput n (List.ofFn r)))) (X.X n) 0

/-- **Computational indistinguishability** `{X_n} ≈ {Y_n}` [PS10, Definition 69.4], headline
form: for every non-uniform PPT `D`, the advantage
`|Pr[t ← X_n : D(1^n, t) = 1] − Pr[t ← Y_n : D(1^n, t) = 1]|` is a negligible function of
`n`. (The text's "there exists a negligible `ε` with advantage `< ε(n)` for all `n`" is
equivalent, `indist_iff_exists_negligible`.)

**Deviation:** `D` receives `1^n` in addition to the sample (D5); the literal form is
`IndistLit`, and the two are related by `Indist.toLit` and `IndistLit.toIndist`. -/
def Indist (X Y : Ensemble ℓ) : Prop :=
  ∀ D : NUPPT, Negligible fun n => distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n))

/-- **Computational indistinguishability, literal form** [PS10, Definition 69.4]: the
distinguisher receives the sample `t` only, i.e. is activated at parameter `|t| = ℓ(n)`
(`D_{|t|}(t)` in the machine-sequence reading of [PS10, Definition 26.8]). -/
def IndistLit (X Y : Ensemble ℓ) : Prop :=
  ∀ D : NUPPT, Negligible fun n =>
    distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher (ℓ.eval n) (ℓ.eval n))

/-- A **pseudorandom ensemble** [PS10, Definition 74.1]: indistinguishable from the uniform
ensemble `{U_{ℓ(n)}}`. -/
def Pseudorandom (X : Ensemble ℓ) : Prop := Indist X (uniform ℓ)

/-- The defining property of `Pseudorandom`: `X.Pseudorandom ↔ Indist X (uniform ℓ)`. -/
theorem pseudorandom_iff (X : Ensemble ℓ) : X.Pseudorandom ↔ Indist X (uniform ℓ) := Iff.rfl

/-- The image ensemble `{M(X_n)}` of [PS10, Lemma 71.5]: at parameter `n`, draw a seed of `X`
and coins for `M`, run `M(1^n, X_n)` and pad or truncate the output to `ℓ'(n)` bits. The
output length `ℓ'` is an explicit syntactic polynomial so that the padding is itself
polynomial-time (`polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly`). The padding (`padFin`: `false`-padding or
truncation) is lossless when `M` outputs exactly `ℓ'(n)` bits, the only case Definition 69.4
can type (a sufficient condition), and can be lossy otherwise (`[1]` and `[1, 0]` both pad to
`[1, 0, …]`; gate 03a, round 2, R2-5): variable-length
outputs (ciphertexts, views, transcripts) are not ensembles of this kind. -/
def push (M : NUPPT) (ℓ' : PolyExpr) (X : Ensemble ℓ) : Ensemble ℓ' where
  σ n := X.σ n × M.Coins n
  X n z := padFin (ℓ'.eval n) (M.runAt n (List.ofFn (X.X n z.1)) z.2)

/-- The blockwise bijection `{0,1}^{q·ℓ} ≃ ({0,1}^ℓ)^q` (private copy of the frozen
`FunFamily.blocks` of `Asymptotic/OneWay.lean`, which this file does not import). -/
private def blocks (q ℓ : ℕ) : (Fin (q * ℓ) → Bool) ≃ (Fin q → Fin ℓ → Bool) :=
  (Equiv.arrowCongr finProdFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl Bool)).trans (Equiv.curry _ _ _)

/-- `t(n)` independent copies of `X_n`, concatenated into one `t(n)·ℓ(n)`-bit string: the
ensemble `{X_n^{(1)} ‖ ⋯ ‖ X_n^{(t(n))}}` of the multicopy corollary of the hybrid lemma
[PS10, Lemma 71.6; Gar26, Lemma 3.3]. -/
def copies (t : PolyExpr) (X : Ensemble ℓ) : Ensemble (.mul t ℓ) where
  σ n := Fin (t.eval n) → X.σ n
  X n s := (blocks (t.eval n) (ℓ.eval n)).symm (TCSlib.Cryptography.copies (t.eval n) (X.X n) s)

/-- Unfolding of `copies`: bit `i` of the concatenation is bit `i mod ℓ` of copy `i / ℓ`
(through `finProdFinEquiv`). -/
theorem copies_X (t : PolyExpr) (X : Ensemble ℓ) (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (t.eval n) → X.σ n)
    (i : Fin (t.eval n * ℓ.eval n)) :
    (X.copies t).X n s i = X.X n (s (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).1) (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).2 :=
  rfl

/-- The uniform ensemble is efficiently samplable: `s := ℓ` and the sampler returns its coins
(`pairSndD` of `⟨1^n, r⟩`). Non-vacuity of `Samplable` (the case `U_n` of D6). -/
theorem uniform_samplable (ℓ : PolyExpr) : (uniform ℓ).Samplable := by
  refine ⟨ℓ, pairSndD, polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, fun n => ?_⟩
  have h : (fun r : Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool =>
      padFin (ℓ.eval n) (pairSndD (NUPPT.advInput n (List.ofFn r)))) = (uniform ℓ).X n := by
    funext r
    simp [NUPPT.advInput, padFin_ofFn, uniform]
  rw [h]
  exact StatClose.refl _

end Ensemble

/-! ### The "distinguishes with probability" notations of Definition 69.4 -/

/-- `D` **distinguishes** the distributions `X` and `Y` **with probability `ε`**
[PS10, p. 70, after Definition 69.4]: `|Pr[t ← X : D(t) = 1] − Pr[t ← Y : D(t) = 1]| > ε`. -/
def Distinguishes {σ τ γ ρ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] [Fintype ρ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ)
    (D : γ → ρ → Bool) (ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ε < distAdv X Y D

/-- `D` **distinguishes the ensembles** `{X_n}` and `{Y_n}` **with probability `μ(·)`**
[PS10, p. 70]: for all `n`, `D` distinguishes `X_n` and `Y_n` with probability `μ(n)`. -/
def Ensemble.DistinguishesWith {ℓ : PolyExpr} (X Y : Ensemble ℓ) (D : NUPPT) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ n, Distinguishes (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) (μ n)

/-- The text's form of Definition 69.4 — "there exists a negligible `ε` with advantage
`< ε(n)` for all `n`" — is equivalent to the frozen form "the advantage is negligible"
[PS10, Definition 69.4]: the advantage lies in `[0, 1]`, so one direction is `Negligible.mono`
and the other takes `ε(n) := advantage(n) + 2^{-n}`. -/
theorem Ensemble.indist_iff_exists_negligible {ℓ : PolyExpr} (X Y : Ensemble ℓ) :
    X.Indist Y ↔ ∀ D : NUPPT, ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, Negligible ε ∧
      ∀ n, distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) < ε n := by
  constructor
  · intro h D
    refine ⟨fun n => distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) + (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ n,
      (h D).add negligible_two_pow_neg, fun n => ?_⟩
    have : (0 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ n := by positivity
    linarith
  · intro h D
    obtain ⟨ε, hε, hlt⟩ := h D
    refine hε.mono ⟨0, fun n _ => ?_⟩
    have h0 : 0 ≤ distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) := abs_nonneg _
    rw [abs_of_nonneg h0]
    exact (hlt n).le.trans (le_abs_self _)

/-- **The contradiction idiom of the text** [PS10, §3.1, Lemma 71.5's proof and passim]:
"assume for contradiction that there is a polynomial `p` such that for infinitely many `n` the
advantage is at least `1/p(n)`" is exactly non-negligibility (`not_negligible_iff`), with the
polynomial a syntactic `PolyExpr` with positive values.

**Proof sketch.** (⇒) `not_negligible_iff` gives an exponent `c`; take `p := (n+1)^c`
(`PolyExpr.normal 1 c`), which is positive and dominates `n^c`. (⇐) `p(n) ≤ C(n+1)^c`
(`PolyExpr.eval_le`) and `(n+1)^c ≤ 2^c n^c`, so `p(n) ≤ n^{c+1}` once `n ≥ C·2^c`; the
exponent `c + 1` witnesses `not_negligible_iff`. -/
theorem not_negligible_iff_exists_polyExpr {μ : ℕ → ℝ} :
    ¬ Negligible μ ↔ ∃ p : PolyExpr, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
      ∀ n₀, ∃ n ≥ n₀, 1 / (p.eval n : ℝ) ≤ |μ n| := by
  rw [not_negligible_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨c, hc⟩
    refine ⟨.normal 1 c, fun n => by simp [PolyExpr.eval_normal], fun n₀ => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨n, hn, h⟩ := hc (max n₀ 1)
    refine ⟨n, le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hn, le_trans ?_ h⟩
    have hn1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hn
    rw [PolyExpr.eval_normal]
    push_cast
    rw [one_mul]
    exact one_div_le_one_div_of_le (pow_pos (by linarith) c)
      (pow_le_pow_left₀ (by linarith) (by linarith) c)
  · rintro ⟨p, hp, h⟩
    obtain ⟨C, c, hC⟩ := p.eval_le
    refine ⟨c + 1, fun n₀ => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨n, hn, hμ⟩ := h (max n₀ (C * 2 ^ c + 1))
    refine ⟨n, le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hn, le_trans ?_ hμ⟩
    have hn' : C * 2 ^ c + 1 ≤ n := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hn
    have key : p.eval n ≤ n ^ (c + 1) := by
      calc p.eval n ≤ C * (n + 1) ^ c := hC n
        _ ≤ C * (2 * n) ^ c := by gcongr; omega
        _ = C * 2 ^ c * n ^ c := by rw [mul_pow, mul_assoc]
        _ ≤ n * n ^ c := by gcongr; omega
        _ = n ^ (c + 1) := by ring
    have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < p.eval n := by exact_mod_cast hp n
    exact one_div_le_one_div_of_le hpos (by exact_mod_cast key)

/-! ### Properties of computational indistinguishability [PS10, §3.1.1] -/

/-- **Reflexivity of `≈`** (non-vacuity of `Indist`): every ensemble is indistinguishable
from itself, the advantage being identically zero. -/
theorem Ensemble.Indist.refl {ℓ : PolyExpr} (X : Ensemble ℓ) : X.Indist X := by
  intro D
  have h : (fun n => distAdv (X.X n) (X.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n))) =
      fun _ => (0 : ℝ) := by
    funext n
    simp [distAdv]
  rw [h]
  exact negligible_zero

/-- **Symmetry of `≈`**: the advantage is symmetric in the two distributions. -/
theorem Ensemble.Indist.symm {ℓ : PolyExpr} {X Y : Ensemble ℓ} (h : X.Indist Y) : Y.Indist X := by
  intro D
  have e : (fun n => distAdv (Y.X n) (X.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n))) =
      fun n => distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) :=
    funext fun n => abs_sub_comm _ _
  rw [e]
  exact h D

/-- **Bridge from the `1^n` form to the literal form** of Definition 69.4: if `{X_n} ≈ {Y_n}`
against distinguishers receiving `1^n`, then also against distinguishers receiving the sample
only [PS10, Definition 69.4; D5].

**Proof sketch.** A literal distinguisher `D` activated at parameter `ℓ(n)` is, as a function
of `n`, the activation of the machine `B := NUPPT.exists_reparam D ℓ` (advice
`D.advice (ℓ n)`, coins `D.coins.subst ℓ`), whose `runAtL n t r` equals `D.runAtL (ℓ n) t r`;
`B` ignores `1^n`. The coin types `B.Coins n` and `D.Coins (ℓ n)` correspond along
`PolyExpr.eval_subst` (`finCongr`), so the acceptance probabilities of
`B.distinguisher n (ℓ n)` and `D.distinguisher (ℓ n) (ℓ n)` agree
(`EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_reparam`); hence the two advantage functions are equal and `h B`
gives negligibility. -/
theorem Ensemble.Indist.toLit {ℓ : PolyExpr} {X Y : Ensemble ℓ} (h : X.Indist Y) :
    X.IndistLit Y := by
  intro D
  obtain ⟨B, hBc, -, hB⟩ := D.exists_reparam ℓ
  refine (h B).mono ⟨0, fun n _ => le_of_eq ?_⟩
  congr 1
  unfold distAdv
  rw [EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_reparam hBc hB, EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_reparam hBc hB]

/-- **Bridge from the literal form to the `1^n` form** for injective `ℓ` (every ensemble of
the text): if `{X_n} ≈ {Y_n}` against literal distinguishers, then also against distinguishers
receiving `1^n` [PS10, Definition 69.4; D5].

The hypothesis `hℓ` excludes only constant `ℓ`: a `PolyExpr` has natural-number coefficients,
so `ℓ.eval` is constant or strictly increasing. For constant `ℓ ≡ L` the two forms coincide as
well (not formalized, no consumer): the `2^L` point tests `t ↦ [t = t₀]` are advice-free
literal distinguishers, so `IndistLit` makes `Σ_{t₀} |Pr[X_n = t₀] − Pr[Y_n = t₀]|`, hence the
statistical distance of `X_n` and `Y_n`, negligible, and that bounds every distinguisher
(`distAdv_le_of_statClose`). So D5's "`D` receives `1^n`" costs nothing for ensembles.

**Proof sketch.** `ℓ.eval` is monotone (`PolyExpr.eval_mono`) and injective, hence strictly
increasing, so `n ≤ ℓ n` for all `n`. Let `φ m := n` if `m = ℓ n` (`Classical.choose` of the
preimage, unique by injectivity) and `φ m := 0` off the image; then `φ m ≤ m`, so
`NUPPT.exists_reparam_advice D φ .var` gives a machine `B` with coins `D.coins.subst var =
D.coins` that at parameter `m = ℓ n` runs `D` at parameter `φ m = n` on its first
`D.coinLen n` coins, with the advice `⟨1^n, D.advice n⟩` hard-wired at length `ℓ n`. Hence
`B.distinguisher (ℓ n) (ℓ n)` and `D.distinguisher n (ℓ n)` have equal advantages after
discarding the unread coins (`EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_reparam_advice`: the coin split
`EnsembleLemmas.coinsEquiv` built on `Fin.appendEquiv`, then
`EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_coins_fst`), and `h B` gives negligibility. -/
theorem Ensemble.IndistLit.toIndist {ℓ : PolyExpr} {X Y : Ensemble ℓ}
    (hℓ : Function.Injective ℓ.eval) (h : X.IndistLit Y) : X.Indist Y := by
  classical
  intro D
  have hsm : StrictMono ℓ.eval := ℓ.eval_mono.strictMono_of_injective hℓ
  have hle : ∀ n, n ≤ ℓ.eval n := fun n => hsm.id_le n
  let φ : ℕ → ℕ := fun m => if hm : ∃ n, ℓ.eval n = m then hm.choose else 0
  have hφ : ∀ m, φ m ≤ PolyExpr.var.eval m := by
    intro m
    simp only [φ, PolyExpr.eval_var]
    split_ifs with hm
    · exact (hle _).trans_eq hm.choose_spec
    · exact Nat.zero_le _
  have hφn : ∀ n, φ (ℓ.eval n) = n := by
    intro n
    have hm : ∃ n', ℓ.eval n' = ℓ.eval n := ⟨n, rfl⟩
    simp only [φ, dif_pos hm]
    exact hℓ hm.choose_spec
  obtain ⟨A, hAc, hA⟩ := D.exists_reparam_advice φ .var hφ
  refine (h A).mono ⟨0, fun n _ => le_of_eq ?_⟩
  congr 1
  have hle' : D.coinLen (φ (ℓ.eval n)) ≤ D.coinLen (PolyExpr.var.eval (ℓ.eval n)) := by
    rw [hφn, PolyExpr.eval_var]
    exact D.coins.eval_mono (hle n)
  unfold distAdv
  rw [EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_reparam_advice hAc hA (ℓ.eval n) hle',
    EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_reparam_advice hAc hA (ℓ.eval n) hle', hφn]

/-- **Closure under efficient operations** [PS10, Lemma 71.5]: if `{X_n} ≈ {Y_n}` then for every
non-uniform PPT `M` (and every explicit output length `ℓ'`), `{M(X_n)} ≈ {M(Y_n)}`.

**Proof sketch.** Fix a distinguisher `D` of the image ensembles. The machine
`D' := EnsembleLemmas.exists_pushRed M D ℓ'` (coins `M.coins + D.coins`, advice
`combineAdvice (M.advice n) (D.advice n)`, built as `NUPPT.ofPolyTime` of a raw function of
the layout `⟨⟨⟨1^n, t⟩, α⟩, r⟩` as in `NUPPT.exists_seq`) runs `M` on `t` with the first
`M.coins n` coins, pads the result to `ℓ'(n)` bits *inside the layout*, where `1^n` is
available (`NUPPT.exists_comp` sees only `y`, gate 03a finding 3; the padding is
`EnsembleLemmas.polyTimeComputable_padL`, a typed cut `pairTakePoly ℓ'` of the output
followed by `0^{ℓ'(n)}`), and hands it to `D` with the remaining coins. Its distinguisher at
`n` is the concrete `sunglassRed P (D.distinguisher n (ℓ' n))` with
`P t c := padFin (ℓ' n) (M.runAt n (ofFn t) c)` up to the coin split
`EnsembleLemmas.coinsEquiv` (`Fin.appendEquiv`), so by `acceptProb_bind`
(`EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_pushRed`) its acceptance probabilities on `X_n`, `Y_n` are those
of `D` on `pushSampler P (X.X n) = (X.push M ℓ').X n` and `(Y.push M ℓ').X n`. Hence the
advantage function of `D` on the images is that of `D'` on `X, Y`, negligible by `h D'`. -/
theorem Ensemble.Indist.push {ℓ ℓ' : PolyExpr} {X Y : Ensemble ℓ} (h : X.Indist Y) (M : NUPPT) :
    (X.push M ℓ').Indist (Y.push M ℓ') := by
  intro D
  obtain ⟨B, hBc, hB⟩ := EnsembleLemmas.exists_pushRed M D ℓ'
  refine (h B).mono ⟨0, fun n _ => le_of_eq ?_⟩
  congr 1
  unfold distAdv
  rw [EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_pushRed hBc hB (X := X.X n),
    EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_pushRed hBc hB (X := Y.X n)]
  rfl

/-- **The hybrid lemma** [PS10, Lemma 71.6], at one parameter: if `D` distinguishes `X^0` and
`X^m` with advantage `ε` then some consecutive pair `X^i, X^{i+1}` (`i < m`) is distinguished
by `D` with advantage at least `ε / m`. (The text indexes `X^1, …, X^m` and loses the factor
`m` where `m − 1` steps would do; harmless.) This is the concrete `exists_hybrid_gap` applied to
the acceptance probabilities `g_i = Pr[t ← X^i : D(t) = 1]`. All hybrids share one seed type
`σ` (`X : ℕ → σ → γ`); hybrids with seeds of different shapes are first embedded into a
common product seed. -/
theorem hybrid_lemma {σ γ ρ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype ρ] {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m)
    (X : ℕ → σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    ∃ i < m, distAdv (X 0) (X m) D / m ≤ distAdv (X i) (X (i + 1)) D := by
  obtain ⟨i, hi, h⟩ := exists_hybrid_gap (fun i => acceptProb (X i) D) hm
  exact ⟨i, hi, h⟩

/-- **Transitivity of `≈`** [PS10, §3.1.1, "Transitivity – The Hybrid Lemma"]: the two-step
case of the hybrid lemma. The advantage between `X` and `Z` is at most the sum of the
advantages between `X, Y` and `Y, Z` (triangle inequality), and sums of negligible functions
are negligible. -/
theorem Ensemble.Indist.trans {ℓ : PolyExpr} {X Y Z : Ensemble ℓ} (h₁ : X.Indist Y)
    (h₂ : Y.Indist Z) : X.Indist Z := by
  intro D
  refine ((h₁ D).add (h₂ D)).mono ⟨0, fun n _ => ?_⟩
  have h0 : 0 ≤ distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) +
      distAdv (Y.X n) (Z.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) :=
    add_nonneg (abs_nonneg _) (abs_nonneg _)
  rw [abs_of_nonneg h0]
  unfold distAdv
  rw [abs_abs]
  exact abs_sub_le _ _ _

/-- **Polynomially many copies** (the multicopy corollary of the hybrid lemma,
[PS10, Lemma 71.6; Gar26, Lemma 3.3]): if `{X_n} ≈ {Y_n}` and both ensembles are efficiently
samplable, then `t(n)` independent copies remain indistinguishable for every syntactic
polynomial `t`.

The samplability hypotheses are those of [Gar26, Lemma 3.3]'s uniform reduction, which
samples the other copies (D6). Against non-uniform distinguishers they can be dropped: hard-wire
the hybrid index and the other `t(n) − 1` copies that keep the gap as advice
(`NUPPT.exists_withAdvice`). That form is not proved, since no consumer needs copies of a
non-samplable ensemble (gate 03a, finding 2).

**Proof sketch.** Fix a distinguisher `D` of the `t(n)`-fold products. At each `n` with
`t(n) > 0`, `exists_multicopyRed_ge` (through the block bijection `blocks`) gives a hybrid
index `k_n < t(n)` such that the concrete reduction `multicopyRed (X.X n) (Y.X n) (t n) k_n D'`
(sample `k_n` copies of `Y`, `t(n) − k_n − 1` copies of `X`, plant the challenge at position
`k_n`, call `D` once) has advantage at least `ε(n) / t(n)`; the index is chosen per `n`
(`choose`; for `t(n) = 0` any index, both products being the one-point distribution,
`EnsembleLemmas.distAdv_eq_zero_of_subsingleton`) and `1^{k_n}` is hard-wired into the
advice (`NUPPT.exists_withAdvice`). The reduction is the `NUPPT` of
`EnsembleLemmas.exists_copiesRed`: the `Samplable` evaluators of `X` and `Y` are run on the
`t(n)` chunks of fresh coins by the state loop `EnsembleLemmas.CopiesLoop`
(`polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit`, coins cut by `pairTakePoly`/`pairDropPoly`, the challenge
planted at the hard-wired position), and `D` is called through `NUPPT.exists_seq`. The laws
of the sampled copies equal the ideal `X.X n`, `Y.X n` (`StatClose … 0`, lifted to the product
by `EnsembleLemmas.statClose_copies` and `StatClose.prod`), so the acceptance probabilities
coincide exactly (`EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_multicopyRed_congr`). Hence
`distAdv ((X.copies t).X n) ((Y.copies t).X n) D ≤ t(n) · distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) B_n` with
the reduction `B` independent of `n` up to the advice, and `t(n) ≤ C (n+1)^c`
(`PolyExpr.eval_le`) makes the right-hand side negligible
(`EnsembleLemmas.negligible_polyExpr_mul`, from `Negligible.mul_pow` and
`Negligible.const_mul`); `Negligible.mono` concludes. -/
theorem Ensemble.Indist.copies {ℓ : PolyExpr} {X Y : Ensemble ℓ} (h : X.Indist Y)
    (hX : X.Samplable) (hY : Y.Samplable) (t : PolyExpr) :
    (X.copies t).Indist (Y.copies t) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨sX, SX, hSX, hXc⟩ := hX
  obtain ⟨sY, SY, hSY, hYc⟩ := hY
  intro D
  -- the distinguisher of `t(n)`-tuples behind `D`
  obtain ⟨D', hD'⟩ : ∃ D' : ∀ n, (Fin (t.eval n) → Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool) → D.Coins n → Bool,
      ∀ n v r, D' n v r = D.distinguisher n ((PolyExpr.mul t ℓ).eval n)
        ((EnsembleLemmas.blocks (t.eval n) (ℓ.eval n)).symm v) r := ⟨_, fun _ _ _ => rfl⟩
  have hadv : ∀ n, distAdv ((X.copies t).X n) ((Y.copies t).X n)
      (D.distinguisher n ((PolyExpr.mul t ℓ).eval n)) =
      distAdv (TCSlib.Cryptography.copies (t.eval n) (X.X n))
        (TCSlib.Cryptography.copies (t.eval n) (Y.X n)) (D' n) := by
    intro n
    have e : ∀ Z : Ensemble ℓ, acceptProb ((Z.copies t).X n)
        (D.distinguisher n ((PolyExpr.mul t ℓ).eval n)) =
        acceptProb (TCSlib.Cryptography.copies (t.eval n) (Z.X n)) (D' n) := by
      intro Z
      refine OneWay.uprob_congr fun z => ?_
      rw [hD']
      exact Iff.rfl
    unfold distAdv
    rw [e, e]
  -- the hybrid index at each `n` (any index when `t(n) = 0`)
  have hex : ∀ n, ∃ k, k ≤ t.eval n ∧ (0 < t.eval n → k < t.eval n ∧
      distAdv (TCSlib.Cryptography.copies (t.eval n) (X.X n))
        (TCSlib.Cryptography.copies (t.eval n) (Y.X n)) (D' n) / t.eval n ≤
        distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (multicopyRed (X.X n) (Y.X n) (t.eval n) k (D' n))) := by
    intro n
    by_cases ht : 0 < t.eval n
    · obtain ⟨k, hk, hge⟩ := exists_multicopyRed_ge (X.X n) (Y.X n) ht (D' n)
      exact ⟨k, hk.le, fun _ => ⟨hk, hge⟩⟩
    · exact ⟨0, Nat.zero_le _, fun h' => absurd h' ht⟩
  choose k hk using hex
  obtain ⟨B, hBc, hB⟩ := EnsembleLemmas.exists_copiesRed D hSX hSY sX sY ℓ t k fun n => (hk n).1
  -- the machine's advantage is the concrete reduction's advantage
  have hBadv : ∀ n, distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (B.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) =
      distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (multicopyRed (X.X n) (Y.X n) (t.eval n) (k n) (D' n)) := by
    intro n
    have hlen : B.coinLen n = (t.eval n * sX.eval n + t.eval n * sY.eval n) + D.coinLen n := by
      simp [NUPPT.coinLen, hBc]
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ : ∃ e : ((Fin (t.eval n) → Fin (sX.eval n) → Bool) ×
        (Fin (t.eval n) → Fin (sY.eval n) → Bool)) × D.Coins n ≃ B.Coins n,
        ∀ c, e c = EnsembleLemmas.coinsEquiv hlen
          (EnsembleLemmas.coinsEquiv rfl ((EnsembleLemmas.blocks _ _).symm c.1.1,
            (EnsembleLemmas.blocks _ _).symm c.1.2), c.2) :=
      ⟨((((EnsembleLemmas.blocks _ _).symm.prodCongr (EnsembleLemmas.blocks _ _).symm).trans
        (EnsembleLemmas.coinsEquiv rfl)).prodCongr (Equiv.refl _)).trans
          (EnsembleLemmas.coinsEquiv hlen), fun _ => rfl⟩
    have hpt : ∀ (z : Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool) c, B.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n) z (e c) =
        multicopyRed
          (fun r : Fin (sX.eval n) → Bool => padFin (ℓ.eval n) (SX (NUPPT.advInput n (List.ofFn r))))
          (fun r : Fin (sY.eval n) → Bool => padFin (ℓ.eval n) (SY (NUPPT.advInput n (List.ofFn r))))
          (t.eval n) (k n) (D' n) z c := by
      intro z c
      rw [he]
      simp only [NUPPT.distinguisher, NUPPT.runAt_eq, EnsembleLemmas.ofFn_coinsEquiv, hB,
        multicopyRed, hD']
    have hdist : ∀ Z : Ensemble ℓ, acceptProb (Z.X n) (B.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) =
        acceptProb (Z.X n) (multicopyRed (X.X n) (Y.X n) (t.eval n) (k n) (D' n)) := by
      intro Z
      rw [← EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_coins_equiv e, ← EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_multicopyRed_congr
        (hXc n) (hYc n)]
      congr 1
      funext z c
      exact hpt z c
    unfold distAdv
    rw [hdist, hdist]
  -- the hybrid bound at each `n`
  have hbound : ∀ n, distAdv ((X.copies t).X n) ((Y.copies t).X n)
      (D.distinguisher n ((PolyExpr.mul t ℓ).eval n)) ≤
      (t.eval n : ℝ) * distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (B.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) := by
    intro n
    rw [hBadv, hadv]
    by_cases ht : 0 < t.eval n
    · obtain ⟨-, hk2⟩ := (hk n).2 ht
      have htR : (0 : ℝ) < t.eval n := by exact_mod_cast ht
      rw [div_le_iff₀ htR] at hk2
      linarith
    · have ht0 : t.eval n = 0 := Nat.eq_zero_of_not_pos ht
      have hsub : Subsingleton (Fin (t.eval n) → Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool) := by
        rw [ht0]
        infer_instance
      rw [EnsembleLemmas.distAdv_eq_zero_of_subsingleton]
      exact mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) (abs_nonneg _)
  refine (EnsembleLemmas.negligible_polyExpr_mul t (h B)).mono ⟨0, fun n _ => ?_⟩
  have h₁ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ distAdv ((X.copies t).X n) ((Y.copies t).X n)
      (D.distinguisher n ((PolyExpr.mul t ℓ).eval n)) := abs_nonneg _
  have h₂ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ distAdv (X.X n) (Y.X n) (B.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) := abs_nonneg _
  rw [abs_of_nonneg h₁, abs_of_nonneg (mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) h₂)]
  exact hbound n

/-! ### Distinguishing versus predicting [PS10, p. 73, Lemma 73.8] -/

/-- The sampler of the prediction experiment `b ← {0,1}; t ← X^b_n` [PS10, Lemma 73.8]: output
the bit `b` together with a sample of `X¹_n` if `b = 1` and of `X⁰_n` otherwise (both seeds are
drawn; the unused one is ignored). -/
def mixEnsemble {ℓ : PolyExpr} (X₀ X₁ : Ensemble ℓ) (n : ℕ) :
    Bool × (X₀.σ n × X₁.σ n) → Bool × (Fin (ℓ.eval n) → Bool) :=
  fun z => (z.1, if z.1 then X₁.X n z.2.2 else X₀.X n z.2.1)

/-- **Predicting is distinguishing** — the identity behind [PS10, p. 73 ("any such predictor
would be a valid distinguisher (show this!)") and the proof of Lemma 73.8]: for samplers
`X⁰, X¹` and any `D` (used as a predictor of the bit `b` in `b ← {0,1}; t ← X^b`),
`Pr[D(t) = b] = 1/2 + (Pr[D(X¹) = 1] − Pr[D(X⁰) = 1]) / 2`. In particular a predictor with
success `1/2 + δ` is a distinguisher with advantage `2δ`, and conversely.

**Repair (run-3 audit P2-2):** the seed types and the coin type carry `Nonempty` instances
(with an empty `ρ`, `σ₀` or `σ₁` the left-hand side is the probability over an empty space,
`0`, while the right-hand side is `1/2`); for ensemble seeds (`Ensemble.nonempty`) and machine
coins (`Fin k → Bool`) they are found by instance resolution.

**Proof sketch.** Split on `b` (`uprob_bool_prod` after regrouping the sample space): for
`b = 1` the event is `D(X¹) = 1`, for `b = 0` it is `D(X⁰) ≠ 1`, whose probability is
`1 − Pr[D(X⁰) = 1]` (`uprob_not`); the unused seed is an ignored uniform coordinate
(`acceptProb_fst`, `acceptProb_snd`). -/
theorem predict_eq {ℓ : ℕ} {σ₀ σ₁ ρ : Type*} [Fintype σ₀] [Fintype σ₁] [Fintype ρ]
    [Nonempty σ₀] [Nonempty σ₁] [Nonempty ρ]
    (X₀ : σ₀ → (Fin ℓ → Bool)) (X₁ : σ₁ → (Fin ℓ → Bool)) (D : (Fin ℓ → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    uprob (fun z : (Bool × (σ₀ × σ₁)) × ρ =>
        D (if z.1.1 then X₁ z.1.2.2 else X₀ z.1.2.1) z.2 = z.1.1) =
      1 / 2 + (acceptProb X₁ D - acceptProb X₀ D) / 2 := by
  rw [← uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodAssoc Bool (σ₀ × σ₁) ρ).symm, uprob_bool_prod]
  have hA : uprob (fun c : (σ₀ × σ₁) × ρ => D (X₀ c.1.1) c.2 = false) =
      1 - acceptProb X₀ D := by
    rw [← acceptProb_fst (τ := σ₁) X₀ D, acceptProb, ← uprob_not]
    congr 1
    funext c
    simp
  have hB : uprob (fun c : (σ₀ × σ₁) × ρ => D (X₁ c.1.2) c.2 = true) = acceptProb X₁ D := by
    rw [← acceptProb_snd (τ := σ₀) X₁ D]
    rfl
  simp only [Equiv.prodAssoc_symm_apply, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, if_true]
  rw [hA, hB]
  ring

/-- **The prediction lemma** [PS10, Lemma 73.8]: if a non-uniform PPT `D` distinguishes
`{X⁰_n}` and `{X¹_n}` with probability `μ(n)` for infinitely many `n`, then there is a
non-uniform PPT `A` with `Pr[b ← {0,1}; t ← X^b_n : A(1^n, t) = b] > 1/2 + μ(n)/2` for
infinitely many `n`.

**Repair (run-3 audit P2-2):** the ad hoc hypotheses `h₀ h₁ : ∀ n, Nonempty (X.σ n)` of the
run-2 statement were dropped; they are the field `Ensemble.nonempty`, and the frozen shape of
DESIGN.md §2.11 is restored.

**Proof sketch.** By `predict_eq` at each `n`, `D` itself predicts with probability
`1/2 + (Pr[D(X¹) = 1] − Pr[D(X⁰) = 1]) / 2` and the negated machine `D'` (output `[true]`
iff `D`'s output is not `[true]`: `EnsembleLemmas.exists_negRed`, i.e. `NUPPT.exists_comp`
with the FP-level `polyTimeComputable_ite` on `pairEq`) predicts with probability
`1/2 − (Pr[D(X¹) = 1] − Pr[D(X⁰) = 1]) / 2`. On the infinite set of `n` where
`μ(n) < |Pr[D(X¹) = 1] − Pr[D(X⁰) = 1]|`, the sign of the difference is positive infinitely
often or negative infinitely often (pigeonhole on an infinite set, no advice needed); take
`A := D` in the first case and `A := D'` in the second. The seed-space reindexing between the
experiment of the statement and `predict_eq` is `uprob_comp_equiv`. -/
theorem prediction_lemma {ℓ : PolyExpr} (X₀ X₁ : Ensemble ℓ) (D : NUPPT) (μ : ℕ → ℝ)
    (h : ∀ n₀, ∃ n ≥ n₀, μ n < distAdv (X₀.X n) (X₁.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n))) :
    ∃ A : NUPPT, ∀ n₀, ∃ n ≥ n₀, 1 / 2 + μ n / 2 <
      uprob fun z : (Bool × (X₀.σ n × X₁.σ n)) × A.Coins n =>
        A.predictor n (ℓ.eval n) (mixEnsemble X₀ X₁ n z.1).2 z.2 = (mixEnsemble X₀ X₁ n z.1).1 := by
  -- the signed advantage of `D`
  obtain ⟨δ, hδ⟩ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ n, δ n = acceptProb (X₁.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) -
      acceptProb (X₀.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) := ⟨_, fun _ => rfl⟩
  have hkey : ∀ n, distAdv (X₀.X n) (X₁.X n) (D.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) = |δ n| := fun n => by
    rw [hδ]
    exact abs_sub_comm _ _
  -- predicting is distinguishing, for any machine `A`
  have hpred : ∀ (A : NUPPT) n, (uprob fun z : (Bool × (X₀.σ n × X₁.σ n)) × A.Coins n =>
      A.predictor n (ℓ.eval n) (mixEnsemble X₀ X₁ n z.1).2 z.2 = (mixEnsemble X₀ X₁ n z.1).1) =
      1 / 2 + (acceptProb (X₁.X n) (A.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n)) -
        acceptProb (X₀.X n) (A.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n))) / 2 := fun A n =>
    predict_eq (X₀.X n) (X₁.X n) (A.distinguisher n (ℓ.eval n))
  by_cases hpos : ∀ n₀, ∃ n ≥ n₀, μ n < δ n
  · -- the difference is positive infinitely often: `D` itself predicts
    refine ⟨D, fun n₀ => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨n, hn, hlt⟩ := hpos n₀
    refine ⟨n, hn, ?_⟩
    rw [hpred, ← hδ]
    linarith
  · -- otherwise it is negative infinitely often: the negated machine predicts
    push_neg at hpos
    obtain ⟨n₁, hn₁⟩ := hpos
    have hneg : ∀ n₀, ∃ n ≥ n₀, μ n < -δ n := by
      intro n₀
      obtain ⟨n, hn, hlt⟩ := h (max n₀ n₁)
      refine ⟨n, le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hn, ?_⟩
      have h1 := hn₁ n (le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hn)
      rw [hkey] at hlt
      rcases le_or_gt 0 (δ n) with h0 | h0
      · rw [abs_of_nonneg h0] at hlt
        linarith
      · rw [abs_of_neg h0] at hlt
        exact hlt
    obtain ⟨A, hAc, hA⟩ := EnsembleLemmas.exists_negRed D
    refine ⟨A, fun n₀ => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨n, hn, hlt⟩ := hneg n₀
    refine ⟨n, hn, ?_⟩
    rw [hpred, EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_negRed hAc hA, EnsembleLemmas.acceptProb_negRed hAc hA]
    have := hδ n
    linarith

/-! ### The pairwise-independent sampling inequality [PS10, Appendix A, p. 189] -/

/-- **Pairwise-independent sampling inequality** [PS10, Appendix A, p. 189]: for pairwise
independent bits `X_1, …, X_m`, each `true` with probability `p`, and `ε > 0`,
`Pr[|∑ᵢ X_i / m − p| ≥ ε] ≤ 1 / (4 ε² m)`. The concrete lemma is
`HardcoreBit.chebyshev_pairwise_ident` [Gar26, Theorem 2.4], restated with the empirical mean.

**Deviation:** the text states the inequality for real random variables with `|X_i| ≤ 1` and
mean `μ` with the bound `(1 − μ²)/(m ε²)`; here the variables are bits (the only case used in
the campaign) and the bound is the variance bound `p(1−p) ≤ 1/4` of the concrete layer. Bits
satisfy the text's hypothesis, and `1/4 > 1 − p²` exactly when `p > √3/2`, so for such `p`
this bound is weaker than the text's (at `p = 1` the text gives `0`); the variance form
`p(1−p)/(m ε²)` would imply both. -/
theorem pairwise_sampling_ineq {Ω ι : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω] [Fintype ι]
    {X : ι → Ω → Bool} (hX : HardcoreBit.PairwiseIndep X) {p : ℝ}
    (hp : ∀ i, uprob (fun ω => X i ω = true) = p) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hm : 0 < Fintype.card ι) :
    uprob (fun ω => ε ≤ |(∑ i, HardcoreBit.ind (X i ω)) / Fintype.card ι - p|) ≤
      1 / (4 * ε ^ 2 * Fintype.card ι) := by
  have hm' : (0 : ℝ) < Fintype.card ι := by exact_mod_cast hm
  refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ (HardcoreBit.chebyshev_pairwise_ident hX hp hε hm)
  apply OneWay.uprob_congr
  intro ω
  rw [show (∑ i, HardcoreBit.ind (X i ω)) / (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) - p =
      (∑ i, HardcoreBit.ind (X i ω) - p * Fintype.card ι) / Fintype.card ι by
        field_simp, abs_div, abs_of_pos hm', le_div_iff₀ hm']

end TCSlib.Cryptography
