import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PRFLemmas

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The GGM reduction as a non-uniform PPT (machine infrastructure for Theorem 97.3)

The machine behind the last paragraph of the proof of [PS10, Theorem 97.3] ("queries to
`HHF^j` can be emulated in p.p.t. … it follows by closure under efficient operations that `D`
contradicts the pseudorandom property of `g`"): from a next-query oracle machine `D`
(foundation decision D7 of `PassShelatChapter2-4Plan.md`), the evaluator `E` of the
length-doubling generator, a query budget `q` and hybrid indices `i, j` (non-uniform advice),
a `Complexity.NUPPT` `ggmRedMachine` whose verdict on a challenge `z ∈ {0,1}^{2n}` is exactly
the verdict of the concrete sub-hybrid distinguisher `ggmBitsDist (G n) D^{(q n)} (q n) i j`
of the Garg layer (`TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Functions.GGM`). The identity is proved
in `ggmRedMachine_distinguisher`; `TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PRF` wraps it into
`exists_ggmBitsDist_nuppt` (Thm-97.3.3).

**The machine.** On the raw layout `⟨⟨⟨1^n, z⟩, ⟨⟨1^i, 1^j⟩, α_D⟩⟩, W₀ ‖ W₁ ‖ r⟩` (advice: the
two indices in unary and `D`'s advice; coins: `q n` fresh `n`-bit seeds `W₀`, `q n` fresh
`2n`-bit pairs `W₁` and `D`'s coins `r`) it runs a *state loop*
(`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` on the length-guarded step
`Complexity.StateLoop.gstep`) over at most `q n` rounds. The state `⟨H, ⟨T, ⟨1^{|T|}, 1^t⟩⟩⟩`
holds the encoded history `H` of (query, answer) pairs handed to `D`, the lazily sampled table
`T` of (distinct `i`-bit prefix, `2n`-bit value) pairs in order of first appearance
(`QueryTree.noteQuery` / `challengeStream` of the Garg layer) with its size in unary, and the
round counter. A round runs `D` on the history (`Complexity.NUPPT.output`), decodes the move,
looks the prefix of the query up in the table (an inner `iterateFind` loop, `lookup`), draws
the value of a new prefix from the coins — the `k`-th distinct prefix gets `W₁ k` if `k < j`,
the challenge `z` if `k = j` and `E(W₀ k)` otherwise — and answers by walking the lower part
of the tree from the selected half of the value (`ggmEval` of
`TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PRFLemmas`). The loop stops at the first verdict of `D`, or
with the forced verdict `false` after `q n` queries (D7).

**The identity.** The concrete distinguisher is `evalLazy` of the simulated query tree; its
recursion (`concrete_zero`, `concrete_succ`) matches one round of the machine
(`step_enc`), and `concrete_iterate` telescopes the rounds up to the first verdict. The
history of the text's tree is `buildTree` of `TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PRF`; this file
uses the equivalent `Option`-valued form `buildTreeQ` (no `OracleMove`), identified with
`buildTree` in `PRF.lean`.

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.queryOf`, `GGMRed.verdictOf`, `GGMRed.buildTreeQ`,
  `GGMRed.histEnc` — the next-query semantics in `Option` form.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.tblEnc`, `GGMRed.tblOf`, `GGMRed.lookup` — the lazily sampled
  table and its lookup loop.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.stateLoopFun` — the state-loop function (retained input, guarded
  step).
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.step`, `GGMRed.acc`, `GGMRed.out`, `GGMRed.start`,
  `GGMRed.rawFun` — the round, the stopping test, the output and the raw function of the
  reduction machine.

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.stateLoopFun_poly`, `GGMRed.stateLoopFun_eval` — the state loop
  is polynomial-time and evaluates to the output at the first accepted round.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.lookup_poly`, `GGMRed.lookup_tblOf` — the table lookup.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.rawFun_poly` — the raw function of the reduction machine is
  polynomial-time.

The evaluation of the machine on its genuine input, the machine itself (`ggmRedMachine`) and
the functional identity with `ggmBitsDist` are in
`TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.GGMReductionEval`.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§3.8.3, proof of Theorem 97.3, last paragraph.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.4.2 (proof of Theorem 3.3, the outer adversary `B`, footnote 9
  on lazy sampling).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed

open Complexity Turing Finset QueryTree

/-! ## The next-query semantics in `Option` form -/

/-- The query decoded from a machine output: `⟨[false], x⟩` with `x` an `ℓ₁`-bit string is
the query `x`; anything else is `none` (a verdict). -/
def queryOf (ℓ₁ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : Option (Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) :=
  match pairDecode w with
  | some ([false], x) => decodeFin ℓ₁ x
  | _ => none

/-- The defining equation of `queryOf`: `decodeFin ℓ₁ x` when `w` decodes as `⟨[false], x⟩`,
`none` otherwise. -/
theorem queryOf_eq (ℓ₁ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    queryOf ℓ₁ w = match pairDecode w with
      | some ([false], x) => decodeFin ℓ₁ x
      | _ => none := rfl

/-- The verdict read off a machine output that is not a query: `true` iff the output is the
two-bit string `[true, true]`. -/
def verdictOf (w : List Bool) : Bool := decide (w = [true, true])

/-- The defining equation of `verdictOf`: `verdictOf w = decide (w = [true, true])`. -/
theorem verdictOf_eq (w : List Bool) : verdictOf w = decide (w = [true, true]) := rfl

/-- The query tree of a next-query string function `next` with budget `b` from the history
`hist` (`Option` form of `buildTree`): a verdict stops, a query within budget becomes a node,
a query at budget `0` is the forced verdict `false`. -/
def buildTreeQ {ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℕ} (next : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool)) → List Bool) :
    ℕ → List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool)) → QueryTree (Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool) Bool
  | 0, hist => match queryOf ℓ₁ (next hist) with
    | some _ => .ret false
    | none => .ret (verdictOf (next hist))
  | b + 1, hist => match queryOf ℓ₁ (next hist) with
    | some x => .query x (fun o => buildTreeQ next b (hist ++ [(x, o)]))
    | none => .ret (verdictOf (next hist))

/-- Unfolding `buildTreeQ` at budget `0`. -/
theorem buildTreeQ_zero {ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℕ} (next : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool)) → List Bool)
    (hist : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool))) :
    buildTreeQ next 0 hist =
      match queryOf ℓ₁ (next hist) with
      | some _ => .ret false
      | none => .ret (verdictOf (next hist)) := rfl

/-- Unfolding `buildTreeQ` at budget `b + 1`. -/
theorem buildTreeQ_succ {ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℕ} (next : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool)) → List Bool)
    (b : ℕ) (hist : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool))) :
    buildTreeQ next (b + 1) hist =
      match queryOf ℓ₁ (next hist) with
      | some x => .query x (fun o => buildTreeQ next b (hist ++ [(x, o)]))
      | none => .ret (verdictOf (next hist)) := rfl

/-- The encoding of a history of (query, answer) pairs as nested pairs (the same term as
`encodeHist` of `TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PRF`). -/
def histEnc {ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℕ} (h : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool))) : List Bool :=
  h.foldr (fun p acc => pairEncode (pairEncode (List.ofFn p.1) (List.ofFn p.2)) acc) []

/-- The defining equation of `histEnc`: the right fold of `⟨⟨x, o⟩, acc⟩` over the history,
starting from `[]`. -/
theorem histEnc_eq {ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℕ} (h : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool))) :
    histEnc h =
      h.foldr (fun p acc => pairEncode (pairEncode (List.ofFn p.1) (List.ofFn p.2)) acc) [] :=
  rfl

/-- Pairing distributes over a concatenation in the second component. -/
theorem pairEncode_append_right (a b c : List Bool) :
    pairEncode a (b ++ c) = pairEncode a b ++ c := by
  simp [pairEncode_eq_dbl]

/-- The encoding of a history is a flat concatenation: appending one entry appends its
encoding `⟨⟨x, y⟩, []⟩`. -/
theorem histEnc_append_single {ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℕ} (h : List ((Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool)))
    (p : (Fin ℓ₁ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ₂ → Bool)) :
    histEnc (h ++ [p]) = histEnc h ++ pairEncode (pairEncode (List.ofFn p.1) (List.ofFn p.2)) [] := by
  induction h with
  | nil => simp [histEnc]
  | cons e h ih =>
    simp only [List.cons_append, histEnc, List.foldr_cons] at ih ⊢
    rw [ih, pairEncode_append_right]

/-- The length of an encoded history: `6ℓ + 6` bits per entry (`ℓ`-bit queries and answers). -/
theorem length_histEnc {ℓ : ℕ} (h : List ((Fin ℓ → Bool) × (Fin ℓ → Bool))) :
    (histEnc h).length = h.length * (6 * ℓ + 6) := by
  induction h with
  | nil => simp [histEnc]
  | cons e h ih =>
    simp only [histEnc, List.foldr_cons] at ih ⊢
    rw [length_pairEncode, length_pairEncode, ih, List.length_ofFn, List.length_ofFn,
      List.length_cons]
    ring

/-! ## The lazily sampled table -/

/-- The encoding of a table of (prefix, value) string pairs as nested pairs
`⟨⟨p₁, v₁⟩, ⟨⟨p₂, v₂⟩, …, []⟩⟩`. -/
def tblEnc (tbl : List (List Bool × List Bool)) : List Bool :=
  tbl.foldr (fun e acc => pairEncode (pairEncode e.1 e.2) acc) []

/-- The encoding of a table is a flat concatenation: appending one entry appends its
encoding. -/
theorem tblEnc_append_single (tbl : List (List Bool × List Bool)) (e : List Bool × List Bool) :
    tblEnc (tbl ++ [e]) = tblEnc tbl ++ pairEncode (pairEncode e.1 e.2) [] := by
  induction tbl with
  | nil => simp [tblEnc]
  | cons e' tbl ih =>
    simp only [List.cons_append, tblEnc, List.foldr_cons] at ih ⊢
    rw [ih, pairEncode_append_right]

/-- The encoding of a nonempty table is `⟨⟨p, v⟩, rest⟩`. -/
@[simp] theorem tblEnc_cons (e : List Bool × List Bool) (tbl : List (List Bool × List Bool)) :
    tblEnc (e :: tbl) = pairEncode (pairEncode e.1 e.2) (tblEnc tbl) := rfl

/-- The encoding of the empty table is empty. -/
@[simp] theorem tblEnc_nil : tblEnc [] = [] := rfl

/-- A table has at most as many entries as its encoding has bits. -/
theorem length_le_length_tblEnc (tbl : List (List Bool × List Bool)) :
    tbl.length ≤ (tblEnc tbl).length := by
  induction tbl with
  | nil => simp
  | cons e tbl ih =>
    rw [tblEnc_cons, length_pairEncode, List.length_cons]
    omega

/-- The table of the distinct prefixes `L` (typed `i`-bit strings) numbered from `k`, with the
values `val k, val (k+1), …`: the entry of the `m`-th prefix is `(List.ofFn L[m], val (k + m))`. -/
def tblOf {i : ℕ} (val : ℕ → List Bool) : List (Fin i → Bool) → ℕ → List (List Bool × List Bool)
  | [], _ => []
  | p :: L, k => (List.ofFn p, val k) :: tblOf val L (k + 1)

/-- The table of `L ++ [p]` is the table of `L` with one more entry. -/
theorem tblOf_append_single {i : ℕ} (val : ℕ → List Bool) (L : List (Fin i → Bool))
    (p : Fin i → Bool) :
    ∀ k, tblOf val (L ++ [p]) k = tblOf val L k ++ [(List.ofFn p, val (k + L.length))] := by
  induction L with
  | nil => intro k; simp [tblOf]
  | cons p' L ih =>
    intro k
    simp only [List.cons_append, tblOf, ih (k + 1), List.length_cons]
    rw [show k + 1 + L.length = k + (L.length + 1) by omega]

/-- The table has one entry per prefix. -/
@[simp] theorem length_tblOf {i : ℕ} (val : ℕ → List Bool) (L : List (Fin i → Bool)) :
    ∀ k, (tblOf val L k).length = L.length := by
  induction L with
  | nil => intro k; rfl
  | cons p L ih => intro k; simp [tblOf, ih]

/-- The prefixes of the table are the encoded prefixes. -/
theorem tblOf_getElem_fst {i : ℕ} (val : ℕ → List Bool) (L : List (Fin i → Bool)) :
    ∀ (k m : ℕ) (hm : m < (tblOf val L k).length),
      (tblOf val L k)[m].1 = List.ofFn (L[m]'(by simpa using hm)) := by
  induction L with
  | nil => intro k m hm; simp at hm
  | cons p L ih =>
    intro k m hm
    cases m with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ m => exact ih (k + 1) m (by simpa using hm)

/-- The values of the table are `val (k + m)`. -/
theorem tblOf_getElem_snd {i : ℕ} (val : ℕ → List Bool) (L : List (Fin i → Bool)) :
    ∀ (k m : ℕ) (hm : m < (tblOf val L k).length), (tblOf val L k)[m].2 = val (k + m) := by
  induction L with
  | nil => intro k m hm; simp at hm
  | cons p L ih =>
    intro k m hm
    cases m with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ m =>
      simp only [tblOf, List.getElem_cons_succ]
      rw [ih (k + 1) m (by simpa using hm)]
      congr 1
      omega

/-- The length of the encoded table of `L` when every value has `v` bits: `4i + 2v + 6` bits
per entry. -/
theorem length_tblEnc_tblOf {i : ℕ} (val : ℕ → List Bool) {v : ℕ}
    (hval : ∀ k, (val k).length = v) (L : List (Fin i → Bool)) :
    ∀ k, (tblEnc (tblOf val L k)).length = L.length * (4 * i + 2 * v + 6) := by
  induction L with
  | nil => intro k; simp [tblOf]
  | cons p L ih =>
    intro k
    simp only [tblOf, tblEnc_cons, length_pairEncode, List.length_ofFn, hval, ih (k + 1),
      List.length_cons]
    ring


/-! ## State loops with a retained input -/

/-- **The state-loop function** (the function form of the private
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_stateFind` of `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Repetition`): on the
input `x`, run the length-guarded step `Complexity.StateLoop.gstep step B` from `⟨x, start x⟩`
for at most `R|⟨x, start x⟩|` rounds and return `out` of the first state word accepted by `acc`
(`[]` if none). -/
def stateLoopFun (start step : List Bool → List Bool) (acc : List Bool → Bool)
    (out : List Bool → List Bool) (R B : PolyExpr) (x : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  match (List.range (R.eval (pairEncode x (start x)).length + 1)).find?
      (fun i => acc ((StateLoop.gstep step B)^[i] (pairEncode x (start x)))) with
  | some i => out ((StateLoop.gstep step B)^[i] (pairEncode x (start x)))
  | none => []

/-- The state-loop function is polynomial-time (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` on
the guarded step, whose orbit from every word is bounded by `StateLoop.gstepBound B`). -/
theorem stateLoopFun_poly {start step : List Bool → List Bool} {acc : List Bool → Bool}
    {out : List Bool → List Bool} (hstart : PolyTimeComputable start)
    (hstep : PolyTimeComputable step) (hacc : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [acc w])
    (hout : PolyTimeComputable out) (R B : PolyExpr) :
    PolyTimeComputable (stateLoopFun start step acc out R B) := by
  have hF := polyTimeComputable_iterateFind (StateLoop.gstep_poly hstep B) hacc hout R
    (StateLoop.gstepBound B) (fun w i _ => StateLoop.length_gstep_iterate_le step B w i)
  have hpre : PolyTimeComputable fun x => pairEncode x (start x) :=
    polyTimeComputable_id.pairEncode hstart
  exact hF.comp hpre

/-- **Evaluation of the state loop on a good input:** if the test first fires at round
`N ≤ R|x|` and the states of the first `N` rounds fit the bound `B|x|`, the loop returns
`out ⟨x, orbit x N⟩`.

**Proof sketch.** On the genuine orbit the guard never fires (`StateLoop.gstep_iterate_eq`
from the bound on the first `N` states), so the loop's `find?` over
`List.range (R|⟨x, start x⟩| + 1)` — a range containing `N`, as `R` is monotone — returns
`some N` (`StateLoop.find?_range_eq_some`), and the payload is `out ⟨x, orbit x N⟩`. -/
theorem stateLoopFun_eval (start step : List Bool → List Bool) (acc : List Bool → Bool)
    (out : List Bool → List Bool) (R B : PolyExpr) (x : List Bool) (N : ℕ)
    (hN : N ≤ R.eval x.length)
    (hbound : ∀ i ≤ N, (StateLoop.orbit start step x i).length ≤ B.eval x.length)
    (hfirst : ∀ i < N, acc (pairEncode x (StateLoop.orbit start step x i)) = false)
    (hlast : acc (pairEncode x (StateLoop.orbit start step x N)) = true) :
    stateLoopFun start step acc out R B x = out (pairEncode x (StateLoop.orbit start step x N)) := by
  unfold stateLoopFun
  have horb := StateLoop.gstep_iterate_eq start step B x N hbound
  have hle : N ≤ R.eval (pairEncode x (start x)).length :=
    hN.trans (R.eval_mono (by rw [length_pairEncode]; omega))
  have hfind : (List.range (R.eval (pairEncode x (start x)).length + 1)).find?
      (fun i => acc ((StateLoop.gstep step B)^[i] (pairEncode x (start x)))) = some N := by
    apply StateLoop.find?_range_eq_some hle
    · intro i hi
      rw [horb i hi.le]
      exact hfirst i hi
    · rw [horb N le_rfl]
      exact hlast
  rw [hfind]
  show out ((StateLoop.gstep step B)^[N] (pairEncode x (start x))) = _
  rw [horb N le_rfl]

/-! ## The table lookup loop -/

/-- The step of the lookup loop on the word `⟨p, T⟩`: pop the first entry of the table. -/
def lookStep (v : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode (pairFstD v) (pairSndD (pairSndD v))

/-- The acceptance test of the lookup loop: the table is exhausted or its first entry has the
prefix `p`. -/
def lookAcc (v : List Bool) : Bool :=
  decide (pairSndD v = []) || decide (pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD v)) = pairFstD v)

/-- The output of the lookup loop: `[]` if the table is exhausted (not found), else `⟨[], v⟩`
with `v` the value of the first entry. -/
def lookOut (v : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if pairSndD v = [] then [] else pairEncode [] (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD v)))

/-- **The table lookup:** on `⟨p, T⟩` pop entries until the table is exhausted or the first
entry has prefix `p`; at most `|⟨p, T⟩|` rounds (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind`). -/
def lookup (v : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  match (List.range ((PolyExpr.var).eval v.length + 1)).find? (fun k => lookAcc (lookStep^[k] v)) with
  | some k => lookOut (lookStep^[k] v)
  | none => []

/-- The lookup step is polynomial-time. -/
theorem lookStep_poly : PolyTimeComputable lookStep :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)

/-- The lookup test is polynomial-time (`StateLoop.isNil_poly`, `polyTimeComputable_pairEq`,
`StateLoop.or_poly`). -/
theorem lookAcc_poly : PolyTimeComputable fun v => [lookAcc v] := by
  have h1 : PolyTimeComputable fun v => [decide (pairSndD v = [])] :=
    StateLoop.isNil_poly.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have h2 : PolyTimeComputable fun v => [decide (pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD v)) = pairFstD v)] := by
    convert polyTimeComputable_pairEq.comp
      ((polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
        polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)).pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairFstD) using 1
    funext v
    simp
  exact StateLoop.or_poly h1 h2

/-- The lookup output is polynomial-time. -/
theorem lookOut_poly : PolyTimeComputable lookOut := by
  have h1 : PolyTimeComputable fun v => [decide (pairSndD v = [])] :=
    StateLoop.isNil_poly.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  convert polyTimeComputable_ite h1 (polyTimeComputable_const [])
    ((polyTimeComputable_const []).pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
      (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD))) using 1
  funext v
  simp [lookOut]

/-- The orbit of the lookup step from any word stays within two bits of the word.

**Proof sketch.** Every point of the orbit after the first step is a pair `⟨p, T⟩`, and the step
on a pair pops the first entry of `T`, which never lengthens the word; the first step itself adds
at most the two separator bits (a malformed word is turned into `⟨[], []⟩`). -/
theorem length_lookStep_iterate_le (v : List Bool) (k : ℕ) :
    (lookStep^[k] v).length ≤ v.length + 2 := by
  have hpair : ∀ a b : List Bool, (lookStep (pairEncode a b)).length ≤ (pairEncode a b).length := by
    intro a b
    unfold lookStep
    rw [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, length_pairEncode, length_pairEncode]
    have h1 := StateLoop.length_pairFstD_add_pairSndD_le b
    omega
  have hone : (lookStep v).length ≤ v.length + 2 := by
    cases hd : pairDecode v with
    | none =>
      have h1 : pairFstD v = [] := by simp [pairFstD, hd]
      have h2 : pairSndD v = [] := by simp [pairSndD, hd]
      have h3 : pairSndD ([] : List Bool) = [] := rfl
      unfold lookStep
      rw [h1, h2, h3, length_pairEncode]
      simp
    | some ab =>
      obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := ab
      rw [eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode v a b hd]
      exact (hpair a b).trans (Nat.le_add_right _ _)
  cases k with
  | zero => exact Nat.le_add_right _ _
  | succ k =>
    induction k with
    | zero => exact hone
    | succ k ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply' lookStep (k + 1) v]
      refine le_trans ?_ ih
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply' lookStep k v]
      exact hpair (pairFstD (lookStep^[k] v)) (pairSndD (pairSndD (lookStep^[k] v)))

/-- The lookup is polynomial-time (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` with `R = var`
and the orbit bound `var + 2`). -/
theorem lookup_poly : PolyTimeComputable lookup :=
  polyTimeComputable_iterateFind lookStep_poly lookAcc_poly lookOut_poly .var
    (.add .var (.const 2)) (fun v k _ => by
      simpa using length_lookStep_iterate_le v k)

/-- The orbit of the lookup step on `⟨p, tblEnc tbl⟩`: after `k` steps the first `k` entries
are gone. -/
theorem lookStep_iterate_tblEnc (p : List Bool) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (tbl : List (List Bool × List Bool)),
      lookStep^[k] (pairEncode p (tblEnc tbl)) = pairEncode p (tblEnc (tbl.drop k))
  | 0, tbl => by simp
  | k + 1, tbl => by
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    cases tbl with
    | nil =>
      have h : lookStep (pairEncode p (tblEnc [])) = pairEncode p (tblEnc []) := by
        show pairEncode (pairFstD _) (pairSndD (pairSndD _)) = _
        rw [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
        rfl
      rw [h, lookStep_iterate_tblEnc p k []]
      simp
    | cons e tbl =>
      have h : lookStep (pairEncode p (tblEnc (e :: tbl))) = pairEncode p (tblEnc tbl) := by
        simp [lookStep]
      rw [h, lookStep_iterate_tblEnc p k tbl, List.drop_succ_cons]

/-- The lookup test on `⟨p, tblEnc tbl⟩`: the table is empty or its first prefix is `p`. -/
theorem lookAcc_tblEnc (p : List Bool) (tbl : List (List Bool × List Bool)) :
    lookAcc (pairEncode p (tblEnc tbl)) =
      match tbl with
      | [] => true
      | e :: _ => decide (e.1 = p) := by
  cases tbl with
  | nil => simp [lookAcc]
  | cons e tbl =>
    simp only [lookAcc, pairSndD_pairEncode, tblEnc_cons, pairFstD_pairEncode]
    have hne : pairEncode (pairEncode e.1 e.2) (tblEnc tbl) ≠ [] := by
      intro h
      have := congrArg List.length h
      rw [length_pairEncode] at this
      simp at this
    simp [hne]

/-- **The lookup on an encoded table of the distinct prefixes `L`** (with `p` a typed prefix):
`⟨[], val (L.idxOf p)⟩` if `p ∈ L`, else `[]`.

**Proof sketch.** The orbit is `⟨p, tblEnc (tbl.drop k)⟩` (`lookStep_iterate_tblEnc`); the test
fails at round `k < L.idxOf p` because the `k`-th prefix differs from `p`
(`List.not_of_lt_findIdx`, `List.ofFn_injective`) and succeeds at round `L.idxOf p`, where the
table either starts with `p` (`List.getElem_idxOf`) or is exhausted (`List.idxOf_eq_length`);
`StateLoop.find?_range_eq_some` evaluates the `find?`. -/
theorem lookup_tblOf {i : ℕ} (val : ℕ → List Bool) (L : List (Fin i → Bool)) (p : Fin i → Bool) :
    lookup (pairEncode (List.ofFn p) (tblEnc (tblOf val L 0))) =
      if p ∈ L then pairEncode [] (val (L.idxOf p)) else [] := by
  classical
  have hlen : (tblOf val L 0).length = L.length := length_tblOf val L 0
  have hacc : ∀ k, lookAcc (lookStep^[k] (pairEncode (List.ofFn p) (tblEnc (tblOf val L 0)))) =
      match (tblOf val L 0).drop k with
      | [] => true
      | e :: _ => decide (e.1 = List.ofFn p) := by
    intro k
    rw [lookStep_iterate_tblEnc, lookAcc_tblEnc]
  have hidx_le : L.idxOf p ≤ L.length := List.idxOf_le_length
  have hrange : L.idxOf p ≤
      (PolyExpr.var).eval (pairEncode (List.ofFn p) (tblEnc (tblOf val L 0))).length := by
    simp only [PolyExpr.eval_var, length_pairEncode]
    have := length_le_length_tblEnc (tblOf val L 0)
    omega
  have hfirst : ∀ k < L.idxOf p,
      lookAcc (lookStep^[k] (pairEncode (List.ofFn p) (tblEnc (tblOf val L 0)))) = false := by
    intro k hk
    rw [hacc]
    have hkL : k < L.length := lt_of_lt_of_le hk hidx_le
    have hkt : k < (tblOf val L 0).length := by rw [hlen]; exact hkL
    rw [List.drop_eq_getElem_cons hkt]
    simp only
    have hne : L[k] ≠ p := by
      have := List.not_of_lt_findIdx (p := (· == p)) (xs := L) hk
      simpa using this
    rw [tblOf_getElem_fst val L 0 k hkt]
    simp only [decide_eq_false_iff_not]
    intro h
    exact hne (List.ofFn_injective h)
  by_cases hp : p ∈ L
  · have hlt : L.idxOf p < L.length := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem hp
    have hltt : L.idxOf p < (tblOf val L 0).length := by rw [hlen]; exact hlt
    have hlast : lookAcc (lookStep^[L.idxOf p]
        (pairEncode (List.ofFn p) (tblEnc (tblOf val L 0)))) = true := by
      rw [hacc, List.drop_eq_getElem_cons hltt]
      simp only
      rw [tblOf_getElem_fst val L 0 _ hltt]
      simp [List.getElem_idxOf hlt]
    unfold lookup
    rw [StateLoop.find?_range_eq_some hrange hfirst hlast, if_pos hp]
    show lookOut _ = _
    rw [lookStep_iterate_tblEnc, List.drop_eq_getElem_cons hltt]
    simp only [lookOut, pairSndD_pairEncode, tblEnc_cons, pairFstD_pairEncode]
    have hne : pairEncode (pairEncode (tblOf val L 0)[L.idxOf p].1 (tblOf val L 0)[L.idxOf p].2)
        (tblEnc ((tblOf val L 0).drop (L.idxOf p + 1))) ≠ [] := by
      intro h
      have := congrArg List.length h
      rw [length_pairEncode] at this
      simp at this
    rw [if_neg hne, tblOf_getElem_snd val L 0 _ hltt, zero_add]
  · have heq : L.idxOf p = L.length := List.idxOf_eq_length hp
    have hlast : lookAcc (lookStep^[L.idxOf p]
        (pairEncode (List.ofFn p) (tblEnc (tblOf val L 0)))) = true := by
      rw [hacc, List.drop_of_length_le (by rw [hlen, heq])]
    unfold lookup
    rw [StateLoop.find?_range_eq_some hrange hfirst hlast, if_neg hp]
    show lookOut _ = _
    rw [lookStep_iterate_tblEnc, List.drop_of_length_le (by rw [hlen, heq])]
    simp [lookOut]



/-! ## The components of the reduction machine -/

section Machine

variable (E : List Bool → List Bool) (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr)

/-- The retained raw input of the state word `⟨X, S⟩`. -/
def inX (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairFstD w

/-- The state of the state word `⟨X, S⟩`. -/
def inS (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairSndD w

/-- The unary parameter `1^n` of the raw input. -/
def paramU (w : List Bool) : List Bool := NUPPT.inParam (inX w)

/-- The challenge `z` (the argument of the raw input). -/
def chal (w : List Bool) : List Bool := NUPPT.inArg (inX w)

/-- The level index `1^i` (first half of the first advice component). -/
def unI (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairFstD (pairFstD (NUPPT.inAdvice (inX w)))

/-- The sub-hybrid index `1^j` (second half of the first advice component). -/
def unJ (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairSndD (pairFstD (NUPPT.inAdvice (inX w)))

/-- `D`'s advice (second advice component). -/
def advD (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairSndD (NUPPT.inAdvice (inX w))

/-- The whole coin string `W₀ ‖ W₁ ‖ r`. -/
def coinsAll (w : List Bool) : List Bool := NUPPT.inCoins (inX w)

/-- The `q(n)` fresh `n`-bit seeds `W₀` (the first `q(n)·n` coins). -/
def seeds (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (coinsAll w).take ((PolyExpr.mul q .var).eval (paramU w).length)

/-- The coins after the seeds. -/
def coinsRest (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (coinsAll w).drop ((PolyExpr.mul q .var).eval (paramU w).length)

/-- The `q(n)` fresh `2n`-bit pairs `W₁` (the next `q(n)·2n` coins). -/
def pairs (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (coinsRest q w).take ((PolyExpr.mul q (.mul (.const 2) .var)).eval (paramU w).length)

/-- `D`'s coins (the remaining coins). -/
def coinsD (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (coinsRest q w).drop ((PolyExpr.mul q (.mul (.const 2) .var)).eval (paramU w).length)

/-- The encoded history in the state. -/
def hist (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairFstD (inS w)

/-- The encoded table in the state. -/
def tbl (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairFstD (pairSndD (inS w))

/-- The table size `1^{|T|}` in the state. -/
def cnt (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD (inS w)))

/-- The round counter `1^t` in the state. -/
def rnd (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD (inS w)))

/-- `D`'s move on the current history: `D(1^n, H; r)` with `D`'s advice. -/
def move (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  D.output (NUPPT.layout (paramU w) (hist w) (advD w) (coinsD q w))

/-- The move is a query: `⟨[false], x⟩` with `|x| = n`. -/
def isQ (w : List Bool) : Bool :=
  decide (pairFstD (move D q w) = [false]) &&
    decide ((pairSndD (move D q w)).length = (paramU w).length)

/-- The query string `x`. -/
def query (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairSndD (move D q w)

/-- The `i`-bit prefix of the query. -/
def pfx (w : List Bool) : List Bool := (query D q w).take (unI w).length

/-- The table lookup of the prefix. -/
def look (w : List Bool) : List Bool := lookup (pairEncode (pfx D q w) (tbl w))

/-- The unary string `1^{2n}`. -/
def un2 (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate ((PolyExpr.mul (.const 2) .var).eval (paramU w).length) true

/-- The unary product `1^{n·|T|}` (offset of seed number `|T|`). -/
def mul1 (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate ((paramU w).length * (cnt w).length) true

/-- The unary product `1^{2n·|T|}` (offset of pair number `|T|`). -/
def mul2 (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate ((un2 w).length * (cnt w).length) true

/-- The test `|T| < j`. -/
def ltJ (w : List Bool) : Bool := !decide ((unJ w).length ≤ (cnt w).length)

/-- The test `|T| = j`. -/
def eqJ (w : List Bool) : Bool := decide ((cnt w).length = (unJ w).length)

/-- The value of a new (the `|T|`-th distinct) prefix: the pair `W₁ |T|` if `|T| < j`, the
challenge if `|T| = j`, `E(W₀ |T|)` otherwise (`challengeStream`). -/
def fresh (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if ltJ w then ((pairs q w).drop (mul2 w).length).take (un2 w).length
  else if eqJ w then chal w
  else E (((seeds q w).drop (mul1 w).length).take (paramU w).length)

/-- The prefix is not in the table. -/
def notFound (w : List Bool) : Bool := decide (look D q w = [])

/-- The value of the query's prefix: looked up, or fresh. -/
def vstr (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if notFound D q w then fresh E q w else pairSndD (look D q w)

/-- The updated table: a new prefix is appended with its fresh value. -/
def tbl' (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if notFound D q w then tbl w ++ pairEncode (pairEncode (pfx D q w) (fresh E q w)) [] else tbl w

/-- The updated table size. -/
def cnt' (w : List Bool) : List Bool := if notFound D q w then true :: cnt w else cnt w

/-- The label at level `i + 1`: the half of the value selected by bit `x_{i+1}` of the query. -/
def lab (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  selHalf (((query D q w).drop (unI w).length).headD false) (paramU w) (vstr E D q w)

/-- The answer: the walk down the tree from the label along the remaining bits of the query. -/
def ans (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  ggmEval E (pairEncode (lab E D q w) ((query D q w).drop (unI w).length).tail)

/-- The updated history. -/
def hist' (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  hist w ++ pairEncode (pairEncode (query D q w) (ans E D q w)) []

/-- **One round of the reduction machine** on the state word `⟨X, S⟩`. -/
def step (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (hist' E D q w) (pairEncode (tbl' E D q w) (pairEncode (cnt' D q w) (true :: rnd w)))

/-- The query budget `1^{q(n)}`. -/
def unQ (w : List Bool) : List Bool := List.replicate (q.eval (paramU w).length) true

/-- The stopping test: the move is a verdict, or the budget is exhausted. -/
def acc (w : List Bool) : Bool := !(isQ D q w) || decide ((unQ q w).length ≤ (rnd w).length)

/-- The output: the forced verdict `false` on a query (budget exhausted), else `D`'s verdict. -/
def out (w : List Bool) : List Bool := if isQ D q w then [false] else [verdictOf (move D q w)]

/-- The initial state: empty history, empty table, zero counters. -/
def start (_X : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode [] (pairEncode [] (pairEncode [] []))

/-- The orbit bound of the state loop: `q(n)(28n + 27) + 6`. -/
def bound : PolyExpr := .add (.mul q (.add (.mul (.const 28) .var) (.const 27))) (.const 6)

/-- **The raw function of the reduction machine:** the state loop with at most `q(|X|)`
rounds. -/
def rawFun : List Bool → List Bool := stateLoopFun start (step E D q) (acc D q) (out D q) q (bound q)

/-! ### Polynomial time -/

/-- Unary multiplication of two polynomial-time unary lengths
(`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_unaryMul`). -/
theorem unaryMul_poly {f g : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun w => List.replicate ((f w).length * (g w).length) true := by
  obtain ⟨M, c, hM⟩ := Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_unaryMul
  have hmul : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => match pairDecode z with
      | some (u, v) => List.replicate (u.length * v.length) true
      | none => []) := ⟨M, c, 2, hM⟩
  convert hmul.comp (hf.pairEncode hg) using 1
  funext w
  simp [pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- The retained input of the state word is polynomial-time. -/
theorem inX_poly : PolyTimeComputable inX := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
/-- The state of the state word is polynomial-time. -/
theorem inS_poly : PolyTimeComputable inS := polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
/-- The unary parameter is polynomial-time. -/
theorem paramU_poly : PolyTimeComputable paramU := NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inParam.comp inX_poly
/-- The challenge is polynomial-time. -/
theorem chal_poly : PolyTimeComputable chal := NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inArg.comp inX_poly
/-- The level index is polynomial-time. -/
theorem unI_poly : PolyTimeComputable unI :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
    (NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inAdvice.comp inX_poly))
/-- The sub-hybrid index is polynomial-time. -/
theorem unJ_poly : PolyTimeComputable unJ :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
    (NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inAdvice.comp inX_poly))
/-- `D`'s advice is polynomial-time. -/
theorem advD_poly : PolyTimeComputable advD :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp (NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inAdvice.comp inX_poly)
/-- The coin string is polynomial-time. -/
theorem coinsAll_poly : PolyTimeComputable coinsAll := NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_inCoins.comp inX_poly

/-- The seeds are polynomial-time (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly`). -/
theorem seeds_poly : PolyTimeComputable (seeds q) := by
  convert (polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly (.mul q .var)).comp (paramU_poly.pairEncode coinsAll_poly)
    using 1
  funext w
  simp [seeds]

/-- The coins after the seeds are polynomial-time (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly`). -/
theorem coinsRest_poly : PolyTimeComputable (coinsRest q) := by
  convert (polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly (.mul q .var)).comp (paramU_poly.pairEncode coinsAll_poly)
    using 1
  funext w
  simp [coinsRest]

/-- The pairs are polynomial-time. -/
theorem pairs_poly : PolyTimeComputable (pairs q) := by
  convert (polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly (.mul q (.mul (.const 2) .var))).comp
    (paramU_poly.pairEncode (coinsRest_poly q)) using 1
  funext w
  simp [pairs]

/-- `D`'s coins are polynomial-time. -/
theorem coinsD_poly : PolyTimeComputable (coinsD q) := by
  convert (polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly (.mul q (.mul (.const 2) .var))).comp
    (paramU_poly.pairEncode (coinsRest_poly q)) using 1
  funext w
  simp [coinsD]

/-- The encoded history is polynomial-time. -/
theorem hist_poly : PolyTimeComputable hist := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp inS_poly
/-- The encoded table is polynomial-time. -/
theorem tbl_poly : PolyTimeComputable tbl :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp inS_poly)
/-- The table size is polynomial-time. -/
theorem cnt_poly : PolyTimeComputable cnt :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp inS_poly))
/-- The round counter is polynomial-time. -/
theorem rnd_poly : PolyTimeComputable rnd :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp inS_poly))

/-- `D`'s move is polynomial-time (`Complexity.NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_output`). -/
theorem move_poly : PolyTimeComputable (move D q) :=
  D.polyTimeComputable_output.comp
    (NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_layout paramU_poly hist_poly advD_poly (coinsD_poly q))

/-- The query test is polynomial-time (`polyTimeComputable_pairEq`, `polyTimeComputable_lenEq`). -/
theorem isQ_poly : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [isQ D q w] := by
  have h1 : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [decide (pairFstD (move D q w) = [false])] := by
    convert polyTimeComputable_pairEq.comp
      ((polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp (move_poly D q)).pairEncode
        (polyTimeComputable_const [false])) using 1
    funext w
    simp
  have h2 : PolyTimeComputable fun w =>
      [decide ((pairSndD (move D q w)).length = (paramU w).length)] := by
    convert polyTimeComputable_lenEq.comp
      ((polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp (move_poly D q)).pairEncode paramU_poly) using 1
    funext w
    simp
  exact polyTimeComputable_and h1 h2

/-- The query string is polynomial-time. -/
theorem query_poly : PolyTimeComputable (query D q) := polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp (move_poly D q)
/-- The prefix of the query is polynomial-time (`takeLen_poly`). -/
theorem pfx_poly : PolyTimeComputable (pfx D q) := takeLen_poly unI_poly (query_poly D q)
/-- The table lookup is polynomial-time (`lookup_poly`). -/
theorem look_poly : PolyTimeComputable (look D q) := lookup_poly.comp ((pfx_poly D q).pairEncode tbl_poly)
/-- The unary string `1^{2n}` is polynomial-time. -/
theorem un2_poly : PolyTimeComputable un2 := StateLoop.unaryPoly_comp (.mul (.const 2) .var) paramU_poly
/-- The seed offset is polynomial-time (`unaryMul_poly`). -/
theorem mul1_poly : PolyTimeComputable mul1 := unaryMul_poly paramU_poly cnt_poly
/-- The pair offset is polynomial-time (`unaryMul_poly`). -/
theorem mul2_poly : PolyTimeComputable mul2 := unaryMul_poly un2_poly cnt_poly
/-- The test `|T| < j` is polynomial-time. -/
theorem ltJ_poly : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [ltJ w] :=
  StateLoop.not_poly (StateLoop.lenLe_comp cnt_poly unJ_poly)

/-- The test `|T| = j` is polynomial-time. -/
theorem eqJ_poly : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [eqJ w] := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_lenEq.comp (cnt_poly.pairEncode unJ_poly) using 1
  funext w
  simp [eqJ]

/-- The fresh value is polynomial-time (two branches, `takeLen_poly`/`dropLen_poly`, `E`). -/
theorem fresh_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (fresh E q) :=
  polyTimeComputable_ite ltJ_poly (takeLen_poly un2_poly (dropLen_poly mul2_poly (pairs_poly q)))
    (polyTimeComputable_ite eqJ_poly chal_poly
      (hE.comp (takeLen_poly paramU_poly (dropLen_poly mul1_poly (seeds_poly q)))))

/-- The not-found test is polynomial-time. -/
theorem notFound_poly : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [notFound D q w] :=
  StateLoop.isNil_poly.comp (look_poly D q)

/-- The value of the prefix is polynomial-time. -/
theorem vstr_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (vstr E D q) :=
  polyTimeComputable_ite (notFound_poly D q) (fresh_poly E q hE)
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp (look_poly D q))

/-- The updated table is polynomial-time. -/
theorem tbl'_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (tbl' E D q) :=
  polyTimeComputable_ite (notFound_poly D q)
    (tbl_poly.append (((pfx_poly D q).pairEncode (fresh_poly E q hE)).pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_const []))) tbl_poly

/-- The updated table size is polynomial-time. -/
theorem cnt'_poly : PolyTimeComputable (cnt' D q) :=
  polyTimeComputable_ite (notFound_poly D q) ((StateLoop.cons_poly true).comp cnt_poly) cnt_poly

/-- The label is polynomial-time (`selHalf_poly`). -/
theorem lab_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (lab E D q) :=
  selHalf_poly (StateLoop.headBit_poly.comp (dropLen_poly unI_poly (query_poly D q))) paramU_poly
    (vstr_poly E D q hE)

/-- The answer is polynomial-time (`ggmEval_poly`). -/
theorem ans_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (ans E D q) :=
  (ggmEval_poly hE).comp ((lab_poly E D q hE).pairEncode
    (StateLoop.tail_poly.comp (dropLen_poly unI_poly (query_poly D q))))

/-- The updated history is polynomial-time. -/
theorem hist'_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (hist' E D q) :=
  hist_poly.append (((query_poly D q).pairEncode (ans_poly E D q hE)).pairEncode
    (polyTimeComputable_const []))

/-- One round of the machine is polynomial-time. -/
theorem step_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (step E D q) :=
  (hist'_poly E D q hE).pairEncode ((tbl'_poly E D q hE).pairEncode
    ((cnt'_poly D q).pairEncode ((StateLoop.cons_poly true).comp rnd_poly)))

/-- The query budget is polynomial-time (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly`). -/
theorem unQ_poly : PolyTimeComputable (unQ q) := StateLoop.unaryPoly_comp q paramU_poly

/-- The stopping test is polynomial-time. -/
theorem acc_poly : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [acc D q w] :=
  StateLoop.or_poly (StateLoop.not_poly (isQ_poly D q)) (StateLoop.lenLe_comp rnd_poly (unQ_poly q))

/-- The output is polynomial-time (`polyTimeComputable_pairEq` for the verdict). -/
theorem out_poly : PolyTimeComputable (out D q) := by
  have hv : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [verdictOf (move D q w)] := by
    convert polyTimeComputable_pairEq.comp
      ((move_poly D q).pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const [true, true])) using 1
    funext w
    simp [verdictOf]
  exact polyTimeComputable_ite (isQ_poly D q) (polyTimeComputable_const [false]) hv

/-- The initial state is polynomial-time (a constant). -/
theorem start_poly : PolyTimeComputable start :=
  polyTimeComputable_const (pairEncode [] (pairEncode [] (pairEncode [] [])))

/-- **The raw function of the reduction machine is polynomial-time.** -/
theorem rawFun_poly (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) : PolyTimeComputable (rawFun E D q) :=
  stateLoopFun_poly start_poly (step_poly E D q hE) (acc_poly D q) (out_poly D q) q (bound q)

end Machine

end TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.GGMReduction

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The GGM reduction machine and its functional identity (Theorem 97.3, machine step)

The second half of the machine infrastructure for the last paragraph of the proof of
[PS10, Theorem 97.3] (the first half, the components of the state loop and their
polynomial-time proofs, is `TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.GGMReduction`): the concrete
sub-hybrid distinguisher `ggmBitsDist` of the Garg layer as a recursion on rounds
(`concrete`, `pureStep`), the evaluation of the machine's state loop on its genuine input
(`rawFun_rawInput`), the reduction machine `ggmRedMachine` as a `Complexity.NUPPT`, and the
identity `ggmRedMachine_distinguisher` between the machine's verdict and the concrete
distinguisher's verdict.

**The identity.** The concrete distinguisher is `QueryTree.evalLazy` of the simulated query
tree (`levelAdv`, `tableDist` of the Garg layer); its recursion (`concrete_zero`,
`concrete_succ`) matches one round of the machine (`step_eq`: the lookup of the prefix, the
fresh value of a new prefix, the walk down the tree and the extension of the history), and
`concrete_iterate` telescopes the rounds up to the first verdict of `D`. The query tree of the
text is `buildTree` of `TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PRF`; this file uses the equivalent
`Option`-valued form `buildTreeQ`, identified with `buildTree` in `PRF.lean`.

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.Data` — the data of one activation (generator, indices,
  challenge, fresh randomness, `D`'s coins); `GGMRed.rawInput`, `GGMRed.coinStr` — the raw
  input and the coin string of the machine.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.pureStep`, `GGMRed.concrete` — the pure simulation and the
  concrete verdict with a budget.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.encState` — the encoding of a pure state as a machine state.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.ggmRedMachine` — the reduction machine.

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.concrete_iterate` — the recursion of the concrete distinguisher.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.step_eq`, `GGMRed.orbit_eq_encState` — one round of the machine
  on an encoded state, and the closed form of its orbit.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.rawFun_rawInput` — the machine's run on the genuine input.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed.ggmRedMachine_distinguisher` — the machine computes the concrete
  sub-hybrid distinguisher `ggmBitsDist`.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§3.8.3, proof of Theorem 97.3, last paragraph.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.4.2 (proof of Theorem 3.3, the outer adversary `B`, footnote 9
  on lazy sampling).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed

open Complexity Turing Finset QueryTree

/-! ## The concrete distinguisher as a recursion on rounds -/

section Concrete

variable {n : ℕ} (next : List ((Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) → List Bool)
  {P : Type} [DecidableEq P] (π : (Fin n → Bool) → P)
  (ans : (Fin n → Bool) → (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) → Fin n → Bool)
  (a : ℕ → (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool))

/-- The pure state of the simulation: the history handed to `D` and the list of distinct
prefixes seen so far. -/
abbrev PureState (n : ℕ) (P : Type) : Type := List ((Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) × List P

/-- One round of the simulation on the pure state: a query `x` is answered through the lazily
sampled table (`QueryTree.noteQuery`, position `idxOf`) and appended to the history; a verdict
leaves the state unchanged. -/
def pureStep (s : PureState n P) : PureState n P :=
  match queryOf n (next s.1) with
  | some x => (s.1 ++ [(x, ans x (a ((noteQuery s.2 (π x)).idxOf (π x))))], noteQuery s.2 (π x))
  | none => s

/-- The concrete distinguisher's verdict from the pure state with budget `b`: the lazy
evaluation of the simulated tree. -/
def concrete (b : ℕ) (s : PureState n P) : Bool :=
  ((buildTreeQ next b s.1).simulate π ans).evalLazy a s.2

/-- The round is a query round. -/
def IsQ (s : PureState n P) : Prop := ∃ x, queryOf n (next s.1) = some x

/-- Budget `0`: a query is the forced verdict `false`, otherwise the verdict of `D`. -/
theorem concrete_zero (s : PureState n P) :
    concrete next π ans a 0 s =
      match queryOf n (next s.1) with
      | some _ => false
      | none => verdictOf (next s.1) := by
  unfold concrete
  rw [buildTreeQ_zero]
  cases queryOf n (next s.1) <;> rfl

/-- Budget `b + 1`: a query round continues with budget `b` from the next pure state. -/
theorem concrete_succ (b : ℕ) (s : PureState n P) :
    concrete next π ans a (b + 1) s =
      match queryOf n (next s.1) with
      | some _ => concrete next π ans a b (pureStep next π ans a s)
      | none => verdictOf (next s.1) := by
  unfold concrete pureStep
  rw [buildTreeQ_succ]
  cases queryOf n (next s.1) with
  | none => rfl
  | some x => rfl

/-- **Telescoping the rounds:** if the first `t` rounds are query rounds, the concrete verdict
with budget `t + b` is the verdict with budget `b` from the pure state after `t` rounds. -/
theorem concrete_iterate :
    ∀ (t b : ℕ) (s : PureState n P),
      (∀ t' < t, IsQ next ((pureStep next π ans a)^[t'] s)) →
      concrete next π ans a (t + b) s = concrete next π ans a b ((pureStep next π ans a)^[t] s)
  | 0, b, s, _ => by rw [Nat.zero_add]; rfl
  | t + 1, b, s, hq => by
    rw [show t + 1 + b = (t + b) + 1 by omega, concrete_succ, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hq 0 (Nat.succ_pos t)
    simp only [Function.iterate_zero, id] at hx
    rw [hx]
    exact concrete_iterate t b _ fun t' ht' => by
      have := hq (t' + 1) (by omega)
      rwa [Function.iterate_succ_apply] at this

/-- The history grows by at most one entry per round, and the prefix list stays at most as
long as the history. -/
theorem pureStep_length (s : PureState n P) (h : s.2.length ≤ s.1.length) :
    (pureStep next π ans a s).2.length ≤ (pureStep next π ans a s).1.length ∧
      (pureStep next π ans a s).1.length ≤ s.1.length + 1 := by
  unfold pureStep
  cases queryOf n (next s.1) with
  | none => exact ⟨h, Nat.le_succ _⟩
  | some x =>
    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton]
    have := length_noteQuery_le s.2 (π x)
    omega

/-- Along the pure evolution from the empty state, the prefix list is at most as long as the
history, which has at most one entry per round. -/
theorem pureStep_iterate_length (t : ℕ) :
    ((pureStep next π ans a)^[t] ([], [])).2.length ≤
        ((pureStep next π ans a)^[t] ([], [])).1.length ∧
      ((pureStep next π ans a)^[t] ([], [])).1.length ≤ t := by
  induction t with
  | zero => simp
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    have h := pureStep_length next π ans a ((pureStep next π ans a)^[t] ([], [])) ih.1
    omega

end Concrete


/-! ## Decoding queries -/

/-- `decodeFin ℓ w = some x` iff `w` is the encoding of `x`. -/
theorem decodeFin_eq_some_iff (ℓ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (x : Fin ℓ → Bool) :
    decodeFin ℓ w = some x ↔ w = List.ofFn x := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hw : w.length = ℓ := length_eq_of_decodeFin_eq_some h
    simp only [decodeFin, dif_pos hw, Option.some.injEq] at h
    subst h
    refine List.ext_get (by simp [hw]) fun i h₁ h₂ => ?_
    simp
  · rintro rfl
    exact decodeFin_ofFn x

/-- `queryOf` recognises exactly the pairs `⟨[false], x⟩` with `x` an `ℓ`-bit string. -/
theorem queryOf_eq_some_iff (ℓ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (x : Fin ℓ → Bool) :
    queryOf ℓ w = some x ↔ pairDecode w = some ([false], List.ofFn x) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    unfold queryOf at h
    split at h
    next x' hx' => rw [hx', (decodeFin_eq_some_iff ℓ x' x).1 h]
    next => simp at h
  · intro h
    unfold queryOf
    rw [h]
    exact decodeFin_ofFn x

/-- The encoding of the padding of a string of the right length is the string. -/
theorem ofFn_padFin_of_length {ℓ : ℕ} {w : List Bool} (h : w.length = ℓ) :
    List.ofFn (padFin ℓ w) = w := by
  refine List.ext_getElem (by simp [h]) fun k hk₁ hk₂ => ?_
  simp [padFin, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hk₂]

/-- A machine output is a query iff its first component is `[false]` and its second has
length `ℓ`. -/
theorem exists_queryOf_iff (ℓ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    (∃ x, queryOf ℓ w = some x) ↔ pairFstD w = [false] ∧ (pairSndD w).length = ℓ := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    rw [queryOf_eq_some_iff] at hx
    simp [pairFstD, pairSndD, hx]
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    cases hd : pairDecode w with
    | none => simp [pairFstD, hd] at h1
    | some ab =>
      obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := ab
      simp only [pairFstD, pairSndD, hd, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some] at h1 h2
      subst h1
      exact ⟨padFin ℓ b, (queryOf_eq_some_iff ℓ w _).2 (by rw [hd, ofFn_padFin_of_length h2])⟩

/-- The query string of a query move. -/
theorem pairSndD_of_queryOf {ℓ : ℕ} {w : List Bool} {x : Fin ℓ → Bool}
    (h : queryOf ℓ w = some x) : pairSndD w = List.ofFn x := by
  rw [queryOf_eq_some_iff] at h
  simp [pairSndD, h]

/-! ## Evaluation on the genuine input -/

/-- The data of one activation of the reduction at parameter `n`: the generator, the hybrid
indices, the challenge, the fresh randomness of the lazily sampled tables and `D`'s coins. -/
structure Data (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The length-doubling generator at parameter `n`. -/
  G : (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (2 * n) → Bool
  /-- The level index `i`. -/
  i : ℕ
  /-- The sub-hybrid index `j`. -/
  j : ℕ
  /-- The challenge `z ∈ {0,1}^{2n}`. -/
  z : Fin (2 * n) → Bool
  /-- The fresh seeds `W₀` and pairs `W₁` of the lazily sampled tables. -/
  W : (Fin (q.eval n) → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin (q.eval n) → (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool))
  /-- `D`'s coins. -/
  r : D.Coins n

section Eval

variable {D : NUPPT} {q : PolyExpr} {n : ℕ} (d : Data D q n)

/-- The coin string of the machine: the `q(n)` seeds, the `q(n)` pairs (each a `2n`-bit
string), and `D`'s coins. -/
def coinStr : List Bool :=
  List.ofFn ((FunFamily.blocks (q.eval n) n).symm d.W.1) ++
    (List.ofFn ((FunFamily.blocks (q.eval n) (2 * n)).symm fun k => splitHalves.symm (d.W.2 k)) ++
      List.ofFn d.r)

/-- The defining equation of `coinStr`: the seed blocks, then the pair blocks, then `D`'s
coins. -/
theorem coinStr_eq : coinStr d =
    List.ofFn ((FunFamily.blocks (q.eval n) n).symm d.W.1) ++
      (List.ofFn ((FunFamily.blocks (q.eval n) (2 * n)).symm fun k => splitHalves.symm (d.W.2 k)) ++
        List.ofFn d.r) := rfl

/-- The raw input of the machine at parameter `n`: `⟨⟨⟨1^n, z⟩, ⟨⟨1^i, 1^j⟩, α_D⟩⟩, coins⟩`. -/
def rawInput : List Bool :=
  NUPPT.layout (List.replicate n true) (List.ofFn d.z)
    (pairEncode (pairEncode (List.replicate d.i true) (List.replicate d.j true)) (D.advice n))
    (coinStr d)

/-- The answer stream of the concrete distinguisher: `challengeStream` at index `j` with the
split challenge. -/
noncomputable def stream : ℕ → (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) :=
  challengeStream (splitHalves ∘ d.G) d.j (splitHalves d.z) d.W

/-- The stored value strings: the `k`-th distinct prefix stores the `2n`-bit string whose
halves are `stream k`. -/
noncomputable def valStr (k : ℕ) : List Bool := List.ofFn (splitHalves.symm (stream d k))

/-- The next-query function of `D` with the fixed coins `r`. -/
def nextQ (hist : List ((Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool))) : List Bool :=
  D.runAt n (histEnc hist) d.r

/-- The prefix map of the level-`i` simulation. -/
def prefMap (x : Fin n → Bool) : Fin d.i → Bool := prefixAt x d.i

/-- The answer map of the level-`i` simulation. -/
def ansMap (hi : d.i < n) (x : Fin n → Bool) (v : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) :
    Fin n → Bool :=
  ggmFrom (splitHalves ∘ d.G) x (d.i + 1) (pairSel (x ⟨d.i, hi⟩) v)

/-- The encoding of a pure state at round `t`: encoded history, encoded table, table size and
round counter in unary. -/
noncomputable def encState (s : PureState n (Fin d.i → Bool)) (t : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (histEnc s.1) (pairEncode (tblEnc (tblOf (valStr d) s.2 0))
    (pairEncode (List.replicate s.2.length true) (List.replicate t true)))

/-- Every stored value has `2n` bits. -/
theorem length_valStr (k : ℕ) : (valStr d k).length = 2 * n := List.length_ofFn

/-- The initial state encodes the empty pure state at round `0`. -/
theorem start_rawInput : start (rawInput d) = encState d ([], []) 0 := rfl

/-- The length of an encoded state. -/
theorem length_encState (s : PureState n (Fin d.i → Bool)) (t : ℕ) :
    (encState d s t).length =
      2 * (s.1.length * (6 * n + 6)) + 2 +
        (2 * (s.2.length * (4 * d.i + 2 * (2 * n) + 6)) + 2 + (2 * s.2.length + 2 + t)) := by
  simp only [encState, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate, length_histEnc,
    length_tblEnc_tblOf (valStr d) (length_valStr d)]

/-- The length of the raw input is at least `n`. -/
theorem le_length_rawInput : n ≤ (rawInput d).length := by
  simp only [rawInput, NUPPT.layout, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
  omega

variable (s : PureState n (Fin d.i → Bool)) (t : ℕ)

/-- The parameter slot of the encoded state word. -/
theorem paramU_eq : paramU (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.replicate n true := by
  simp [paramU, inX, rawInput]

/-- The challenge slot of the encoded state word. -/
theorem chal_eq : chal (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.ofFn d.z := by
  simp [chal, inX, rawInput]

/-- The level index of the encoded state word. -/
theorem unI_eq : unI (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.replicate d.i true := by
  simp [unI, inX, rawInput]

/-- The sub-hybrid index of the encoded state word. -/
theorem unJ_eq : unJ (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.replicate d.j true := by
  simp [unJ, inX, rawInput]

/-- `D`'s advice in the encoded state word. -/
theorem advD_eq : advD (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = D.advice n := by
  simp [advD, inX, rawInput]

/-- The coins of the encoded state word. -/
theorem coinsAll_eq : coinsAll (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = coinStr d := by
  simp [coinsAll, inX, rawInput]

/-- The seeds of the encoded state word. -/
theorem seeds_eq : seeds q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
    List.ofFn ((FunFamily.blocks (q.eval n) n).symm d.W.1) := by
  rw [seeds, coinsAll_eq, paramU_eq, coinStr]
  simp only [List.length_replicate, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  exact List.take_left' List.length_ofFn

/-- The coins after the seeds of the encoded state word. -/
theorem coinsRest_eq : coinsRest q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
    List.ofFn ((FunFamily.blocks (q.eval n) (2 * n)).symm fun k => splitHalves.symm (d.W.2 k)) ++
      List.ofFn d.r := by
  rw [coinsRest, coinsAll_eq, paramU_eq, coinStr]
  simp only [List.length_replicate, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  exact List.drop_left' List.length_ofFn

/-- The pairs of the encoded state word. -/
theorem pairs_eq : pairs q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
    List.ofFn ((FunFamily.blocks (q.eval n) (2 * n)).symm fun k => splitHalves.symm (d.W.2 k)) := by
  rw [pairs, coinsRest_eq, paramU_eq]
  simp only [List.length_replicate, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  exact List.take_left' List.length_ofFn

/-- `D`'s coins in the encoded state word. -/
theorem coinsD_eq : coinsD q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.ofFn d.r := by
  rw [coinsD, coinsRest_eq, paramU_eq]
  simp only [List.length_replicate, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  exact List.drop_left' List.length_ofFn

/-- The history of the encoded state word. -/
theorem hist_eq : hist (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = histEnc s.1 := by
  simp [hist, inS, encState]

/-- The table of the encoded state word. -/
theorem tbl_eq : tbl (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
    tblEnc (tblOf (valStr d) s.2 0) := by
  simp [tbl, inS, encState]

/-- The table size of the encoded state word. -/
theorem cnt_eq : cnt (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
    List.replicate s.2.length true := by
  simp [cnt, inS, encState]

/-- The round counter of the encoded state word. -/
theorem rnd_eq : rnd (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.replicate t true := by
  simp [rnd, inS, encState]

/-- The move of the machine on the encoded state is `D`'s move on the history. -/
theorem move_eq : move D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = nextQ d s.1 := by
  rw [move, paramU_eq, hist_eq, advD_eq, coinsD_eq]
  rfl

/-- The query test of the machine is the query test of the pure state. -/
theorem isQ_iff : isQ D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = true ↔ IsQ (nextQ d) s := by
  rw [isQ, move_eq, paramU_eq, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq, decide_eq_true_eq,
    List.length_replicate, IsQ, exists_queryOf_iff]

/-- The stopping test on the encoded state. -/
theorem acc_eq : acc D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
    (!isQ D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) || decide (q.eval n ≤ t)) := by
  rw [acc, unQ, paramU_eq, rnd_eq]
  simp only [List.length_replicate]

/-- The output on the encoded state. -/
theorem out_eq : out D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
    if isQ D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) then [false]
    else [verdictOf (nextQ d s.1)] := by
  rw [out, move_eq]

/-- The unary offset of the next seed. -/
theorem mul1_length : (mul1 (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t))).length = n * s.2.length := by
  simp [mul1, paramU_eq, cnt_eq]

/-- The unary string `1^{2n}` of the encoded state word. -/
theorem un2_length : (un2 (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t))).length = 2 * n := by
  simp [un2, paramU_eq]

/-- The unary offset of the next pair. -/
theorem mul2_length :
    (mul2 (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t))).length = (2 * n) * s.2.length := by
  simp [mul2, un2_length, cnt_eq]

/-- **The fresh value is the stored value of the next distinct prefix:** on the encoded state
with `|L| < q(n)`, `fresh` computes `valStr |L|`.

**Proof sketch.** The tests of the machine read `|L| < j` and `|L| = j` off the unary strings;
`challengeStream` unfolds by the same cases. For `|L| < j` the machine reads block `|L|` of the
pairs (`drop_take_ofFn_blocks`), which is `W₁ |L|` re-encoded; for `|L| = j` it returns the
challenge; otherwise it applies `E` to block `|L|` of the seeds, which is `G (W₀ |L|)` by
`hG`. -/
theorem fresh_eq (E : List Bool → List Bool)
    (hG : ∀ s : Fin n → Bool, E (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (d.G s)) (hk : s.2.length < q.eval n) :
    fresh E q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = valStr d s.2.length := by
  have hlt : ltJ (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = decide (s.2.length < d.j) := by
    simp only [ltJ, unJ_eq, cnt_eq, List.length_replicate, ← decide_not, not_le]
  have heq : eqJ (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = decide (s.2.length = d.j) := by
    simp [eqJ, unJ_eq, cnt_eq]
  have hstream : ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k < q.eval n), stream d k =
      if k < d.j then d.W.2 ⟨k, hk⟩ else if k = d.j then splitHalves d.z
        else splitHalves (d.G (d.W.1 ⟨k, hk⟩)) := by
    intro k hk
    simp [stream, challengeStream, extendStream, hk]
  rw [fresh, hlt, heq, valStr, hstream _ hk]
  by_cases h1 : s.2.length < d.j
  · rw [if_pos (by simpa using h1), if_pos h1, pairs_eq, mul2_length, un2_length,
      drop_take_ofFn_blocks (q.eval n) (2 * n) _ hk, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
  · rw [if_neg (by simpa using h1), if_neg h1]
    by_cases h2 : s.2.length = d.j
    · rw [if_pos (by simpa using h2), if_pos h2, chal_eq, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
    · rw [if_neg (by simpa using h2), if_neg h2, seeds_eq, mul1_length, paramU_eq,
        List.length_replicate, drop_take_ofFn_blocks (q.eval n) n _ hk, Equiv.apply_symm_apply,
        hG, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]

/-- **One round of the machine on an encoded query state** is the encoding of the next pure
state.

**Proof sketch.** The move is `D`'s move on the history (`move_eq`), a query `x` whose string
is `List.ofFn x`; its prefix is looked up in the table (`lookup_tblOf`). If the prefix is
known, the stored value is `valStr (idxOf)` and the table is unchanged; otherwise the fresh
value `valStr |L|` (`fresh_eq`) is appended (`tblOf_append_single`, `tblEnc_append_single`) and
the counter grows. In both cases the answer is the walk from the half of the value selected by
bit `x_{i+1}` (`selHalf_ofFn`, `ggmEval_ofFn_walk`, `ggmFrom_eq_walk`), which is the answer map
of the simulation, and the history is extended by `⟨x, answer⟩` (`histEnc_append_single`). -/
theorem step_eq (E : List Bool → List Bool)
    (hG : ∀ s : Fin n → Bool, E (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (d.G s)) (hi : d.i < n)
    (hk : s.2.length < q.eval n) {x : Fin n → Bool} (hx : queryOf n (nextQ d s.1) = some x) :
    step E D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
      encState d (pureStep (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) s) (t + 1) := by
  classical
  have hquery : query D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.ofFn x := by
    rw [query, move_eq, pairSndD_of_queryOf hx]
  have hpfx : pfx D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = List.ofFn (prefixAt x d.i) := by
    rw [pfx, hquery, unI_eq, List.length_replicate, ofFn_prefixAt x hi.le]
  have hlook : look D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
      if prefixAt x d.i ∈ s.2 then pairEncode [] (valStr d (s.2.idxOf (prefixAt x d.i)))
      else [] := by
    rw [look, hpfx, tbl_eq, lookup_tblOf]
  have hbit : ((List.ofFn x).drop d.i).headD false = x ⟨d.i, hi⟩ := by
    rw [List.drop_eq_getElem_cons (by simpa using hi), List.headD_cons, List.getElem_ofFn]
  have hrest : ((List.ofFn x).drop d.i).tail = (List.ofFn x).drop (d.i + 1) := List.tail_drop
  have hans : ∀ k, vstr E D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = valStr d k →
      ans E D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
        List.ofFn (ansMap d hi x (stream d k)) := by
    intro k hv
    rw [ans, lab, hv, hquery, unI_eq, List.length_replicate, hbit, hrest, paramU_eq, valStr,
      selHalf_ofFn _ (List.length_replicate ..) _, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, ggmEval_ofFn_walk hG,
      ansMap, ggmFrom_eq_walk]
  have hpure : pureStep (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) s =
      (s.1 ++ [(x, ansMap d hi x (stream d
        ((noteQuery s.2 (prefixAt x d.i)).idxOf (prefixAt x d.i))))],
        noteQuery s.2 (prefixAt x d.i)) := by
    rw [pureStep, hx]
    rfl
  rw [hpure]
  by_cases hmem : prefixAt x d.i ∈ s.2
  · have hnf : notFound D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = false := by
      simp [notFound, hlook, hmem, Turing.pairEncode_ne_nil]
    have hv : vstr E D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) =
        valStr d (s.2.idxOf (prefixAt x d.i)) := by
      rw [vstr, hnf, hlook, if_pos hmem]
      simp
    rw [noteQuery_of_mem hmem]
    simp only [step, hist', tbl', cnt', hnf, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, hist_eq, tbl_eq,
      cnt_eq, rnd_eq, hquery, hans _ hv]
    simp only [encState, histEnc_append_single, List.replicate_succ]
  · have hnf : notFound D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = true := by
      simp [notFound, hlook, hmem]
    have hv : vstr E D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (encState d s t)) = valStr d s.2.length := by
      rw [vstr, hnf, if_pos rfl, fresh_eq d s t E hG hk]
    have hidx : (noteQuery s.2 (prefixAt x d.i)).idxOf (prefixAt x d.i) = s.2.length := by
      rw [noteQuery_of_not_mem hmem, List.idxOf_append_of_notMem hmem, List.idxOf_cons_self,
        Nat.add_zero]
    rw [hidx, noteQuery_of_not_mem hmem]
    simp only [step, hist', tbl', cnt', hnf, if_true, hist_eq, tbl_eq, cnt_eq, rnd_eq, hquery,
      hans _ hv, hpfx, fresh_eq d s t E hG hk]
    simp only [encState, histEnc_append_single, List.replicate_succ, tblOf_append_single,
      zero_add, tblEnc_append_single, List.length_append, List.length_singleton]

end Eval


/-! ## The run of the machine on the genuine input -/

section Main

variable {D : NUPPT} {q : PolyExpr} {n : ℕ} (d : Data D q n) (E : List Bool → List Bool)
  (hG : ∀ s : Fin n → Bool, E (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (d.G s)) (hi : d.i < n)

/-- The pure state after `t` rounds from the empty state. -/
noncomputable def pureAt (t : ℕ) : PureState n (Fin d.i → Bool) :=
  (pureStep (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d))^[t] ([], [])

/-- The pure state after `t + 1` rounds. -/
theorem pureAt_succ (t : ℕ) :
    pureAt d hi (t + 1) = pureStep (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) (pureAt d hi t) :=
  Function.iterate_succ_apply' _ _ _

/-- The length bounds along the pure evolution. -/
theorem pureAt_length (t : ℕ) :
    (pureAt d hi t).2.length ≤ (pureAt d hi t).1.length ∧ (pureAt d hi t).1.length ≤ t :=
  pureStep_iterate_length (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) t

include hG in
/-- **Closed form of the machine's orbit:** while every earlier round was rejected by the
stopping test (a query round within budget), the state after `t` rounds encodes the pure
state after `t` rounds (`step_eq`). -/
theorem orbit_eq_encState :
    ∀ t, (∀ t' < t, acc D q (pairEncode (rawInput d)
        (StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) t')) = false) →
      StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) t = encState d (pureAt d hi t) t
  | 0, _ => start_rawInput d
  | t + 1, h => by
    have ih := orbit_eq_encState t (fun t' ht' => h t' (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt ht'))
    have hacc := h t (Nat.lt_succ_self t)
    rw [ih, acc_eq] at hacc
    simp only [Bool.or_eq_false_iff, Bool.not_eq_false', decide_eq_false_iff_not, not_le] at hacc
    obtain ⟨hq, ht⟩ := hacc
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (isQ_iff d _ t).1 hq
    have hlen := pureAt_length d hi t
    rw [StateLoop.orbit_succ, ih, step_eq d _ t E hG hi (by omega) hx, pureAt_succ]

include hG hi in
/-- The stopping test fires at some round (at the latest when the budget is exhausted). -/
theorem exists_acc :
    ∃ t, acc D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) t)) =
      true := by
  by_contra hno
  have hfalse : ∀ t, acc D q (pairEncode (rawInput d)
      (StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) t)) = false := by
    intro t
    have := not_exists.1 hno t
    simpa using this
  have h := hfalse (q.eval n)
  rw [orbit_eq_encState d E hG hi (q.eval n) (fun t' _ => hfalse t'), acc_eq] at h
  simp at h

/-- The first accepted round. -/
noncomputable def firstRound : ℕ := Nat.find (exists_acc d E hG hi)

/-- Before the first accepted round the test is `false`. -/
theorem acc_of_lt_firstRound {t : ℕ} (ht : t < firstRound d E hG hi) :
    acc D q (pairEncode (rawInput d) (StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) t)) =
      false := by
  have := Nat.find_min (exists_acc d E hG hi) ht
  simpa using this

/-- The first accepted round is within the budget. -/
theorem firstRound_le : firstRound d E hG hi ≤ q.eval n := by
  by_contra h
  push_neg at h
  have hq := acc_of_lt_firstRound d E hG hi h
  rw [orbit_eq_encState d E hG hi (q.eval n)
    (fun t' ht' => acc_of_lt_firstRound d E hG hi (ht'.trans h)), acc_eq] at hq
  simp at hq

/-- Every round before the first accepted round is a query round of the pure evolution. -/
theorem isQ_of_lt_firstRound {t : ℕ} (ht : t < firstRound d E hG hi) :
    IsQ (nextQ d) (pureAt d hi t) := by
  have h := acc_of_lt_firstRound d E hG hi ht
  rw [orbit_eq_encState d E hG hi t
    (fun t' ht' => acc_of_lt_firstRound d E hG hi (ht'.trans ht)), acc_eq] at h
  simp only [Bool.or_eq_false_iff, Bool.not_eq_false', decide_eq_false_iff_not, not_le] at h
  exact (isQ_iff d _ t).1 h.1

/-- The states of the first `t ≤ q(n)` rounds fit the orbit bound. -/
theorem length_encState_pureAt_le {t : ℕ} (ht : t ≤ q.eval n) :
    (encState d (pureAt d hi t) t).length ≤ (bound q).eval (rawInput d).length := by
  refine le_trans ?_ ((bound q).eval_mono (le_length_rawInput d))
  rw [length_encState]
  have hlen := pureAt_length d hi t
  simp only [bound, PolyExpr.eval_add, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  have hA : (pureAt d hi t).1.length ≤ q.eval n := by omega
  have hB : (pureAt d hi t).2.length ≤ q.eval n := by omega
  have h1 : (pureAt d hi t).1.length * (6 * n + 6) ≤ q.eval n * (6 * n + 6) :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hA
  have h2 : (pureAt d hi t).2.length * (4 * d.i + 2 * (2 * n) + 6) ≤ q.eval n * (8 * n + 6) :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul hB (by omega)
  have hsum : q.eval n * (28 * n + 27) =
      2 * (q.eval n * (6 * n + 6)) + 2 * (q.eval n * (8 * n + 6)) + 3 * q.eval n := by ring
  rw [hsum]
  omega

include hG in
/-- **The machine's raw function on the genuine input is the concrete verdict.**

**Proof sketch.** The state loop stops at the first accepted round `N ≤ q(n)`
(`stateLoopFun_eval` with the closed form `orbit_eq_encState` and the bound
`length_encState_pureAt_le`), where the machine outputs `D`'s verdict or the forced `false`.
Telescoping the concrete recursion over the `N` query rounds (`concrete_iterate`) reduces the
concrete verdict to budget `q(n) − N` at the pure state after `N` rounds: a verdict of `D` is
returned as is (`concrete_zero`, `concrete_succ`), and a query at `N = q(n)` is the forced
`false`. -/
theorem rawFun_rawInput :
    rawFun E D q (rawInput d) =
      [concrete (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) (q.eval n) ([], [])] := by
  have hNq := firstRound_le d E hG hi
  have hfirst : ∀ t < firstRound d E hG hi, acc D q (pairEncode (rawInput d)
      (StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) t)) = false :=
    fun t ht => acc_of_lt_firstRound d E hG hi ht
  have hlast : acc D q (pairEncode (rawInput d)
      (StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) (firstRound d E hG hi))) = true :=
    Nat.find_spec (exists_acc d E hG hi)
  have horbN := orbit_eq_encState d E hG hi (firstRound d E hG hi) hfirst
  have hbound : ∀ t ≤ firstRound d E hG hi,
      (StateLoop.orbit start (step E D q) (rawInput d) t).length ≤
        (bound q).eval (rawInput d).length := by
    intro t ht
    rw [orbit_eq_encState d E hG hi t (fun t' ht' => hfirst t' (lt_of_lt_of_le ht' ht))]
    exact length_encState_pureAt_le d hi (ht.trans hNq)
  have hNR : firstRound d E hG hi ≤ q.eval (rawInput d).length :=
    hNq.trans (q.eval_mono (le_length_rawInput d))
  rw [rawFun, stateLoopFun_eval start (step E D q) (acc D q) (out D q) q (bound q) (rawInput d)
    (firstRound d E hG hi) hNR hbound hfirst hlast, horbN, out_eq]
  have hconc : concrete (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) (q.eval n) ([], []) =
      concrete (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) (q.eval n - firstRound d E hG hi)
        (pureAt d hi (firstRound d E hG hi)) := by
    have h := concrete_iterate (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d)
      (firstRound d E hG hi) (q.eval n - firstRound d E hG hi) ([], [])
      (fun t' ht' => isQ_of_lt_firstRound d E hG hi ht')
    rwa [Nat.add_sub_cancel' hNq] at h
  rw [hconc]
  have hlast' := hlast
  rw [horbN, acc_eq] at hlast'
  by_cases hQ : isQ D q (pairEncode (rawInput d)
      (encState d (pureAt d hi (firstRound d E hG hi)) (firstRound d E hG hi))) = true
  · rw [if_pos hQ]
    have hqN : q.eval n ≤ firstRound d E hG hi := by simpa [hQ] using hlast'
    rw [Nat.sub_eq_zero_of_le hqN, concrete_zero]
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (isQ_iff d _ _).1 hQ
    rw [hx]
  · rw [if_neg hQ]
    have hnone : queryOf n (nextQ d (pureAt d hi (firstRound d E hG hi)).1) = none := by
      rw [Option.eq_none_iff_forall_ne_some]
      intro x hx
      exact hQ ((isQ_iff d _ _).2 ⟨x, hx⟩)
    cases q.eval n - firstRound d E hG hi with
    | zero => rw [concrete_zero, hnone]
    | succ b => rw [concrete_succ, hnone]

end Main

/-! ## The reduction machine -/

/-- The advice-length polynomial of the reduction machine: `2(2n + 2 + q(n)) + 2 + adv_D(n)`. -/
def advPoly (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) : PolyExpr :=
  .add (.mul (.const 2) (.add (.mul (.const 2) .var) (.add (.const 2) q))) (.add (.const 2) D.adv)

/-- The coin polynomial of the reduction machine: `q(n)·n + q(n)·2n + coins_D(n)`. -/
def coinPoly (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) : PolyExpr :=
  .add (.mul q .var) (.add (.mul q (.mul (.const 2) .var)) D.coins)

/-- The advice of the reduction machine: the hybrid indices in unary (clamped to their
ranges, so that the advice is polynomially bounded at every parameter) and `D`'s advice. -/
def adviceOf (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (i j : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (pairEncode (List.replicate (min (i n) n) true)
    (List.replicate (min (j n) (q.eval n)) true)) (D.advice n)

/-- The advice is polynomially bounded. -/
theorem length_adviceOf_le (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (i j : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    (adviceOf D q i j n).length ≤ (advPoly D q).eval n := by
  simp only [adviceOf, advPoly, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate, PolyExpr.eval_add,
    PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  have h1 := D.advice_length n
  have h2 := min_le_right (i n) n
  have h3 := min_le_right (j n) (q.eval n)
  omega

/-- **The reduction machine** of [PS10, proof of Theorem 97.3, last paragraph]: the
non-uniform PPT with advice `⟨⟨1^i, 1^j⟩, α_D⟩`, coins `q(n)·n + q(n)·2n + coins_D`, and raw
function `rawFun` (the state loop hosting `D`'s next-query function). -/
noncomputable def ggmRedMachine {E : List Bool → List Bool} (hE : PolyTimeComputable E)
    (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (i j : ℕ → ℕ) : NUPPT :=
  NUPPT.ofPolyTime (rawFun_poly E D q hE) (coinPoly D q) (advPoly D q) (adviceOf D q i j)
    (length_adviceOf_le D q i j)

/-- The coin polynomial of the reduction machine. -/
@[simp] theorem coins_ggmRedMachine {E : List Bool → List Bool} (hE : PolyTimeComputable E)
    (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (i j : ℕ → ℕ) :
    (ggmRedMachine hE D q i j).coins = coinPoly D q := rfl

/-- The activation of the reduction machine is the raw function on the layout. -/
theorem runAt_ggmRedMachine {E : List Bool → List Bool} (hE : PolyTimeComputable E)
    (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (i j : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (y : List Bool)
    (c : (ggmRedMachine hE D q i j).Coins n) :
    (ggmRedMachine hE D q i j).runAt n y c =
      rawFun E D q (NUPPT.layout (List.replicate n true) y (adviceOf D q i j n) (List.ofFn c)) := by
  show (NUPPT.ofPolyTime (rawFun_poly E D q hE) (coinPoly D q) (advPoly D q) (adviceOf D q i j)
    (length_adviceOf_le D q i j)).runAt n y c = _
  rw [NUPPT.runAt_eq, NUPPT.runAtL_ofPolyTime]
  rfl

/-- **The reduction machine computes the concrete sub-hybrid distinguisher** `ggmBitsDist`
(Thm-97.3.3, functional identity): at a parameter `n` where the hybrid indices are in range,
on the challenge `z` and coins encoding `(W, r)`, the machine's verdict is the verdict of
`ggmBitsDist (G n) D^{(q n)} (q n) i j` on `z` with coins `(W, r)`, where `D^{(q n)}` is the query
tree `buildTreeQ` of `D`'s next-query function.

**Proof sketch.** `runAt_ggmRedMachine` and `rawFun_rawInput` evaluate the machine to the
verdict `concrete … (q n) ([], [])`, which is by definition `evalLazy` of the simulated tree
with the answer stream `challengeStream`, i.e. `ggmBitsDist` unfolded (`ggmDist`, `tableDist`,
`levelAdv`). -/
theorem ggmRedMachine_distinguisher {E : List Bool → List Bool} (hE : PolyTimeComputable E)
    (D : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (i j : ℕ → ℕ) {n : ℕ} (G : (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (2 * n) → Bool)
    (hG : ∀ s : Fin n → Bool, E (List.ofFn s) = List.ofFn (G s)) (hi : i n < n)
    (hj : j n < q.eval n) (z : Fin (2 * n) → Bool)
    (W : (Fin (q.eval n) → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin (q.eval n) → (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)))
    (r : D.Coins n) (c : (ggmRedMachine hE D q i j).Coins n)
    (hc : List.ofFn c = coinStr (⟨G, i n, j n, z, W, r⟩ : Data D q n)) :
    (ggmRedMachine hE D q i j).distinguisher n (2 * n) z c =
      ggmBitsDist G (fun r => buildTreeQ (fun hist => D.runAt n (histEnc hist) r) (q.eval n) [])
        (q.eval n) ⟨i n, hi⟩ ⟨j n, hj⟩ z (W, r) := by
  set d : Data D q n := ⟨G, i n, j n, z, W, r⟩ with hd
  have hraw : NUPPT.layout (List.replicate n true) (List.ofFn z) (adviceOf D q i j n)
      (List.ofFn c) = rawInput d := by
    rw [hc, rawInput, adviceOf, min_eq_left hi.le, min_eq_left hj.le]
  have hdist : (ggmRedMachine hE D q i j).distinguisher n (2 * n) z c =
      decide ([concrete (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) (q.eval n) ([], [])] =
        [true]) := by
    rw [NUPPT.distinguisher, runAt_ggmRedMachine, hraw, rawFun_rawInput d E hG hi]
  have hrhs : ggmBitsDist G (fun r => buildTreeQ (fun hist => D.runAt n (histEnc hist) r)
      (q.eval n) []) (q.eval n) ⟨i n, hi⟩ ⟨j n, hj⟩ z (W, r) =
        concrete (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) (q.eval n) ([], []) := rfl
  rw [hdist, hrhs]
  cases concrete (nextQ d) (prefMap d) (ansMap d hi) (stream d) (q.eval n) ([], []) <;> rfl

end TCSlib.Cryptography.GGMRed
